# Comparing lpc-rs with other LPC drivers

This reference describes differences relevant to choosing a driver or estimating
work on a mudlib port. It covers lpc-rs, CD, LDMud, FluffOS and DGD. Shared LPC
syntax and efun names do not establish compatibility: argument order, callback
context, return values and side effects can differ.

Start with the overview, then the notes for the driver you are coming from:
[CD](#cd), [LDMud](#ldmud), [FluffOS](#fluffos) or [DGD](#dgd).
The shared [`explode` examples](#explode) cover a string-handling gotcha across
all four. [Stored password migration](#stored-passwords) applies to any source
using the supported hash formats. This page is the home for porting advice;
the linked efun, apply, and language references describe native contracts.

## Scope and evidence

The lpc-rs column describes the accompanying code. Upstream sources were reviewed
on **19 September 2026**, against these public snapshots. The revisions identify
the source examined; they are not claims about every release or downstream fork.
Timer ID allocation in CD and FluffOS was additionally reviewed on
**21 September 2026** at the same revisions; it is independent of their optional
callback-player-context settings.
Global timer inspection in FluffOS was source-reviewed on **22 and 24 September 2026**
at the listed revision, with its core call-out efuns enabled. The inspected
implementation returns three fields per timer; no cross-driver execution was
performed. [Implementation][fl-callouts], [declaration][fl-core-spec].
Call-out player preservation was source-reviewed on **28 September 2026** at
these same revisions: FluffOS with its core call-out efuns and `this_player in
call_out` enabled (the runtime default), LDMud's call-out reference, and DGD's
`this_user` reference. FluffOS's shadow traversal is conditional on `NO_SHADOWS`;
its fallback requires an `O_LISTENER` owner. No upstream execution is claimed.
[FluffOS implementation][fl-callouts], [runtime default][fl-runtime-settings],
[LDMud reference][ld-callout-context], [DGD reference][dgd-callout-user].
Timer argument forwarding and lookup were additionally reviewed on
**26 September 2026** at the listed FluffOS revision. These are core efuns;
[Lima's configuration][lima-timer-config] enables `this_player in call_out`.
The event/help adaptations below were exercised on lpc-rs,
without FluffOS execution or a timing comparison.
[Scheduling][fl-callout-reference], [lookup][fl-find-callout].

revision, with `NO_SNOOP` undefined and `receive snoop` enabled (as in the
reviewed Lima configuration). Callback and relationship behavior below comes
from source review, not cross-driver execution. [Connection code][fl-snoop].

The FluffOS `clonep` reference was reviewed on **26 September 2026** at the

performed. [Reference][fl-clonep], [declaration][fl-core-spec].

Unless labelled not checked, entries below are **source-reviewed**: compared with
documentation or implementation, with links to the evidence. No cross-driver execution tests
were run for this page. **Not checked** means no conclusion has been reached;
**not implemented** describes a known absence in the reviewed implementation.
Optional packages, compiler defines and runtime modes can change an upstream
build's behaviour; relevant conditions are stated alongside the feature.
Support implemented in a mudlib or optional package counts too, with that
requirement stated. Disabled by default does not mean unsupported, and a feature
omitted from a selected inventory should not be read as absent.

FluffOS is compared at its own revision, rather than treated as interchangeable
with historical MudOS. DGD's separately distributed multicore relative Hydra is
outside this comparison; the [DGD README][dgd-readme] distinguishes them.

## Overview

These cells describe selected capabilities, not complete feature inventories.
A source link supports each reviewed upstream claim. The
[protocol table](#client-protocols-and-transports) compares individual protocols
across all five drivers; the broader rows describe differences within each area.

| Area | lpc-rs | CD | LDMud | FluffOS | DGD |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Execution | Parallel LPC tasks; snapshot reads, atomic commits and conflict retries. [Runtime](../README.md#how-execution-works); [monotonic elapsed VM uptime](efun/uptime.md). | Tasks evaluated serially by the [backend loop][cd-backend]. | Sequential [backend evaluation][ld-backend]; explicit [coroutines][ld-async]. | Event-driven LPC; [async functions and promises][fl-async], with worker-thread I/O in the async package. | Explicit [atomic functions][dgd-lpc] roll back on errors; multicore acceleration is a separate [Hydra offering][dgd-readme]. |
| Process resource usage | [`rusage()`](efun/rusage.md) returns 16 OS process statistics, with CPU times in milliseconds and peak RSS in KiB; failed or unsupported sampling returns an empty mapping. | **Not checked**. | **Not checked**. | Core `rusage()` returns 16 resource fields, with CPU times in milliseconds and other fields in platform units. [Pinned implementation][fl-rusage-audit-source]. | **Not checked**. |
| Object memory estimates | [`object_memory_info`](efun/object_memory_info.md) returns current object/program/data/total estimates, with transactional reads and sharing/cycle handling. | **Not checked**. | **Not checked**. | Core memory_info(object) includes program, instance data and header; memory_info() uses driver accounting. [Pinned implementation][fl-object-memory-source]. | **Not checked**. |
| Saving and restarting | [Object and mapping save files, including class records](save-format.md), with [`nosave` globals](lpc/nosave.md); [`save_value`](efun/save_value.md) / [`restore_value`](efun/restore_value.md) serialize individual values as strings. Whole-world snapshot/restart is not implemented. | [Object variable saves][cd-save]. | [Object saves][ld-save] with selectable formats and a serialised-string form. | [Object saves][fl-save] with flags, optional compression and a serialised-string form; [`nosave` globals][fl-nosave-keywords] with `SENSIBLE_MODIFIERS`; individual values through [`save_variable`][fl-save-variable] / [`restore_variable`][fl-restore-variable]. | Object saves plus [whole-system snapshots][dgd-dump] and [restart from a snapshot][dgd-intro]. |
| Language features | [Caller inspection](efun/calling_object.md); [Exact int/float comparisons](lpc/comparisons.md); [Configurable zero or distinct nil](lpc/null.md) with [`nilp`](efun/nilp.md); [Type-sensitive array set matching with destroyed-object normalization](lpc/comparisons.md#collection-matching); [`has_key` for mapping membership](efun/has_key.md); [UTF-8 strings, immutable bytes, function values and closures](lpc/types.md); [`evaluate` for values or callbacks](efun/evaluate.md); explicit [value captures](lpc/function_type.md#explicit-value-captures) and [reference parameters](lpc/references.md); [macro argument stringification](lpc/macros.md#stringification) and [predefined source macros](lpc/macros.md#predefined-macros); [pragmas for warnings, include restrictions and retained function types](lpc/pragmas.md); [inheritance visibility, path bases, basename calls, and checked sibling/child function resolution](lpc/inheritance.md); [reverse indices, slices and array/string writes](lpc/indexing.md); [array literal spreading](lpc/array_spreading.md) and [trailing call commas](lpc/anatomy_of_a_program.md#function-calls); [`foreach` with `in` or `:`](lpc/foreach.md); [expression and block catches](efun/catch.md); [named variadic parameters with `mixed` or array collectors](lpc/variadic_parameters.md) and [unnamed prototype parameters](lpc/anatomy_of_a_program.md#function-prototypes); [nominal classes with declaration visibility, shared instances, guarded members, shallow copying and native persistence](lpc/classes.md); [`deep_copy` of mutable container graphs](efun/deep_copy.md); literal [`strindex`](efun/strindex.md), [`replace_string`](efun/replace_string.md) and [`trim`](efun/trim.md); scalar-based string [`member_array`](efun/member_array.md) and [`map`](efun/map.md). | [Function values and partial application][cd-functions]. | [Unicode strings, bytes, structs, lightweight objects and coroutines][ld-types]; [closures][ld-closures], [reference arguments][ld-refs] and [trimming][ld-trim]. | [Unicode text][fl-strings], mutable [buffers][fl-buffer], [function values and closures][fl-functions], [reference parameters][fl-refs], [class declarations][fl-class-grammar], [named variadic parameters][fl-variadic-declarations], [array literal spreading][fl-parameter-grammar], [promises][fl-async], [`copy` with `PACKAGE_CONTRIB`][fl-copy] and [trimming with `PACKAGE_TRIM`][fl-trim]. | [DGD LPC types and modifiers][dgd-lpc]; | Text file writes | [`write_file`](efun/write_file.md) stages append (0/default) or whole-file replacement (1), with pending reads and commit-time delivery. | **Not checked**. | **Not checked**. | Core `write_file` uses bit 1 for overwrite and bit 2 for compression. [Implementation][fluffos-file-write-flags]. | **Not checked**. |
| File metadata | [`file_size`](efun/file_size.md), [`file_time`](efun/file_time.md) and [`get_dir`](efun/get_dir.md); [`mkdir`](efun/mkdir.md) and [`rm`](efun/rm.md) check pending entry changes, and [`rmdir`](efun/rmdir.md) checks pending directory membership without reading file contents. See [Lima adaptations](#lima-file-metadata). | **Not checked**. | **Not checked**. | Core [`stat`][fl-stat-source] combines metadata with loaded-object information or directory results; [`file_length`][fl-file-length] counts LF bytes with `PACKAGE_CONTRIB`. | **Not checked**. |

Async I/O and resumable LPC functions do not by themselves establish parallel
execution of game-state mutations. The lpc-rs runtime's transaction boundary is
the owning driver task, including calls it makes into other objects; its
[transaction diagnostics](transaction-diagnostics.md) describe retries and
execution allowances. Committed external I/O can still fail after state commits.

LDMud's `parse_command` requires the `use-parse-command` build option, enabled in
the reviewed [default settings][ld-settings]. FluffOS's `add_action` requires
`NO_ADD_ACTION` to be unset, as in the reviewed [local options][fl-options];
`parse_command` belongs to the always-enabled `PACKAGE_OPS`, while
`parse_sentence` requires `PACKAGE_PARSER`, enabled by default in the reviewed
[CMake settings][fl-packages].

## Client protocols and transports

**Built in** means the driver handles the protocol's negotiation or framing;
the mudlib still supplies game-specific messages or data. **Mudlib hook** means
the driver exposes a documented interface for implementing that protocol in LPC;
it does not establish that every mudlib implements it. The labels describe where
the protocol is implemented. Client support and the stated server configuration
are required in either case.

**Not in Telnet handler** describes the reviewed driver's built-in handler only.
**Not checked** leaves support unresolved, including mudlibs, extensions and
proxies that have not been reviewed here.

| Protocol or transport | lpc-rs | CD | LDMud | FluffOS | DGD |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Telnet | [Built in](efun/query_connection.md). | [Built in][cd-telnet]. | [Built in][ld-telnet]. | [Built in][fl-config]. | [Built in][dgd-config]. |
| MXP | [Built in](efun/send_mxp.md). | Not in [Telnet handler][cd-telnet]. | [Mudlib hook][ld-telnet]. | Built in; [`enable mxp`][fl-config] (default `0`). | Not checked; see binary-port note below. |
| GMCP | [Built in](efun/send_gmcp.md). | [Built in][cd-network]. | [Mudlib hook][ld-telnet]. | Built in; [`enable gmcp`][fl-config] (default `0`). | Not checked; see binary-port note below. |
| MSSP | [Built in](apply/master/get_mud_stats.md). | [Built in][cd-network]. | [Mudlib hook][ld-telnet]. | Built in; [`enable mssp`][fl-config] (default `1`). | Not checked; see binary-port note below. |
| MCCP compression | [Not implemented](../lpc-rs-telnet/src/session.rs); MCCP2 is refused. | Not in [Telnet handler][cd-telnet]. | [Built in when compiled with MCCP][ld-mccp]; off in the reviewed [default settings][ld-settings]. | [Built-in MCCP2][fl-telnet] on Telnet; WebSocket connections use transport compression instead. | Not checked. |
| MSP sound protocol | No negotiation in the [Telnet session](../lpc-rs-telnet/src/session.rs); mudlib use of sound tags not checked. | Not in [Telnet handler][cd-telnet]; mudlib use of sound tags not checked. | [Mudlib hook][ld-telnet]. | Built in; [`enable msp`][fl-config] (default `1`). | Not checked. |
| TLS | [Built in](secure-connections.md); configure a separate TLS port and certificates. | Not checked. | [Built in when compiled with TLS][ld-tls]; the mudlib calls `tls_init_connection()`. | [Built in][fl-config]; configure `external_port_N_tls` with a certificate and key. | Not checked. |
| WebSocket | [Not implemented by the listener](../src/telnet/listener.rs). | Not checked. | Not checked. | [Built in][fl-config]; configure a `websocket` port and `websocket http dir`. | Not checked. |

LDMud explicitly names MXP, GMCP, MSSP and MSP in its
[`H_TELNET_NEG` contract][ld-telnet]. The hook receives negotiations and
subnegotiations, and [`binary_message`][ld-binary] sends protocol bytes.
This is a supported mudlib integration path; no particular mudlib's protocol
implementation was tested for this comparison.

DGD's [binary ports][dgd-config] deliver data to LPC without its built-in Telnet
processing, allowing a mudlib to handle the wire protocol itself
([connection implementation][dgd-comm], [`send_message`][dgd-send]). Specific
MXP, GMCP or MSSP implementations on that path have not been reviewed here;
the table makes no absence claim about them.

## Differences when porting

These are selected differences, grouped by source driver. They identify places
where a mudlib's expectations need review; they are not a claim that all other
APIs match.

Each driver's section collects its language, efun, apply, and data-migration
notes. Shared topics below avoid repeating the same examples across drivers.
When checking a port, use [apply tracing](apply/master/error_handler.md) to
inspect missing callbacks, argument and result types, and security decisions.

### `explode`

Leading and trailing delimiters, empty input and an empty delimiter can change
both array lengths and field positions when porting. These results follow from
the reviewed sources, with the settings described below; they are not
cross-driver execution-test results.

| Driver / mode | `explode(",a,,b,", ",")` | `explode(",,", ",")` | `explode("", ",")` | `explode("ab", "")` | `explode("", "")` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [lpc-rs](efun/explode.md) | `({ "", "a", "", "b", "" })` | `({ "", "", "" })` | `({ "" })` | `({ "a", "b" })` | `({})` |
| [CD, reviewed defaults][cd-explode] | `({ "", "a", "", "b" })` | `({ "", "" })` | `({})` | `({ "a", "b" })` | `({})` |
| [LDMud][ld-explode] | `({ "", "a", "", "b", "" })` | `({ "", "", "" })` | `({ "" })` | `({ "a", "b" })` | `({ "" })` |
| [FluffOS, reviewed defaults][fl-explode] | `({ "a", "", "b" })` | `({})` | `({})` | `({ "a", "b" })` | `({})` |
| [FluffOS, reversible mode][fl-explode] | `({ "", "a", "", "b", "" })` | `({ "", "", "" })` | `({})` | `({ "a", "b" })` | `({})` |
| [DGD][dgd-explode] | `({ "a", "", "b" })` | `({ "" })` | `({})` | `({ "a", "b" })` | `({})` |

CD's reviewed [configuration][cd-config] leaves both `OLD_EXPLODE` and
`KINGDOMS_EXPLODE` undefined: leading and interior empty fields remain, but the
final empty field is dropped. `KINGDOMS_EXPLODE` changes trailing-field handling;
check the source build's defines before assuming these defaults.

FluffOS defaults to [`sane explode string = 1` and
`reversible explode string = 0`][fl-config]. For input containing non-delimiter
text, that removes one leading and one trailing empty field while keeping
interior empties. With `sane explode string = 0`, all leading empty fields are
removed. `reversible explode string = 1` overrides that trimming; the separate
[`explode_reversible` efun][fl-explode-entry] selects the same reversible path.
Even in reversible mode, empty input returns an empty array and an empty
delimiter adds no boundary fields.

With an empty delimiter, lpc-rs also omits boundary fields and returns an empty
array for empty input. With a nonempty delimiter, lpc-rs retains all empty fields,
including the single empty field for empty input, as LDMud does.

An empty delimiter also exposes different character units: CD and DGD split
into bytes, [LDMud][ld-explode-source] and lpc-rs split text into Unicode scalar
values, and [FluffOS][fl-explode] splits into extended grapheme clusters.
LDMud additionally accepts `bytes` arguments; lpc-rs's `explode` accepts strings
only. A combining mark can therefore be a separate field in lpc-rs while staying
with its base character in FluffOS.

Overlapping multi-character delimiters need review too. The
[FluffOS implementation][fl-explode] processes trailing matches before splitting
the remaining text: `explode("ab---", "--")` returns `({ "ab-" })`, and
`explode_reversible("ab---", "--")` returns `({ "ab-", "" })`. lpc-rs consumes
matches from left to right and returns `({ "ab", "-" })`. Reversible splitting
does not by itself establish identical field boundaries.

Review code that indexes the first or last field, treats an empty array as
"no input", counts characters, or relies on split/join round trips. Preserve
the source driver's intended handling explicitly; filtering every empty field
would also remove meaningful interior fields.

### Stored passwords

For an imported password file using a format supported by [`crypt`](efun/crypt.md),
the check `crypt(password, stored) == stored` can retain its existing meaning.
Classic DES hashes are supported. A mudlib can replace a verified DES hash on
login using the native default SHA-512 format:

```c
if (crypt(p, password) != password)
    return 0;
if (sizeof(password) == 13) {
    password = crypt(p, 0);
    save_me();
}
```

Apply this example only to records identified as classic DES. FluffOS's
[`oldcrypt`][fl-oldcrypt] is a different MudOS algorithm, unsupported by native
`crypt`; its records need a separate migration path. A function rename does not
convert a hash. See the [FluffOS notes](#fluffos).

### CD

| Topic | CD behaviour | lpc-rs behaviour and porting impact |
|---|---|---|
| Array predicate | Calls it `pointerp`. [Reference][cd-pointerp]. | Rename calls to [`arrayp`](efun/arrayp.md), or provide `int pointerp(mixed value) { return arrayp(value); }` as a simul-efun. |
| `reduce` argument order | The callback is first: `reduce(function, mixed, ...)`. [API declarations][cd-api]. | The array is first: `reduce(items, callback, ...)`. Calls and bound arguments in function pointers need the corresponding order. [Reference](efun/reduce.md). |
| Repeating timers | `set_alarm(delay, repeat, callback)`; timer IDs start at `1`. [Reference][cd-alarm], [ID allocation][cd-callouts]. | `call_out(callback, delay, repeat)` registers work at transaction commit; IDs also start at `1`, leaving `0` for an unset handle. The efun name and argument order differ. [Reference](efun/call_out.md). |
| `parse_command` matching | `%s` tries following pattern elements at successive words; destinations are assigned during matching. [Implementation][cd-parse-source]. | `%s` is greedy; destinations change only on a successful match. See the [parser details below](#cd-command-parsing). |
| Regular expressions | A traditional Henry Spencer-derived engine. [Implementation][cd-regexp]. | Rust `regex` syntax, including Unicode classes but no look-around or back-references. Patterns need review even where the efun name matches. [Reference](efun/regexp.md). |
| `save_object` result | Declared `void save_object(string)`. [API declarations][cd-api]. | Returns the save path; the write is deferred to commit. Shared format ancestry does not establish complete interchangeability, particularly for the additional `bytes` encoding. [Efun](efun/save_object.md), [format](save-format.md). |

#### CD command parsing

Review patterns, destination variables, and vocabulary applies together. The
following details come from the pinned [CD parser][cd-parse-source]. The native
[`parse_command`](efun/parse_command.md) reference defines the complete contract;
[`add_rule`](efun/add_rule.md) uses the same native pattern and noun rules.

| Topic | CD behaviour | lpc-rs behaviour and porting impact |
|---|---|---|
| `%s` and `%d` | `%s` searches forward for the next match. `%d` accepts a nonnegative numeric prefix, so `5x` can become `5`. | `%s` is greedy. `%d` requires a digit run that fits an integer; signed or spelled-out numbers do not match that capture. |
| Destination writes | Assigns as matching proceeds; extra captures without destinations are discarded. | Writes destinations only after the entire pattern succeeds; too few destinations raise an error before parsing. |
| Invalid patterns | Warns and skips invalid pattern elements. | Rejects malformed patterns with runtime errors. Review patterns that formerly appeared to work despite warnings. |
| Living lookup | `%l` can fall back to `find_living`. | Searches the supplied scope for objects that called `enable_commands`; there is no global-name fallback. |
| Language defaults | Includes English numeral and plural handling when `PARSE_FOREIGN` is absent. | Numeral words, the all word, and pluralization come from master applies. Supply the mudlib's vocabulary explicitly. |
| Noun vocabulary | Uses object and shared master ID/adjective lists, with a default pluralizer. | Every adjective must be listed and the ID must end the captured phrase. Without an object's `parse_command_id_list()`, the driver asks `id(phrase)`; shared master IDs do not apply to that fallback. |
| Prepositions | Takes the first list entry matching at the current word, without reconsidering it after later failure. | Tries splits until the whole pattern and its noun captures resolve; overlapping entries may select a different result. |

Matching in the native parser is case-sensitive and uses whole words. Test
mudlib assumptions about case normalization at its command-entry boundary.

### LDMud

| Topic | LDMud behaviour | lpc-rs behaviour and porting impact |
|---|---|---|
| Call-out player context | Preserves the scheduling user. [Reference][ld-callout-context]. | Enable `LPC_CALL_OUT_PRESERVE_PLAYER=true`; see the native [`call_out`](efun/call_out.md) contract. |
| String trimming | `trim(text, where, chars)` accepts 1 for left, 2 for right and 0 or 3 for both; the header defines `TRIM_BOTH` as 3. The documented default set is space and tab. [Reference][ld-trim], [header][ld-trim-header]. | Native [`trim`](efun/trim.md) uses 0 for both (the default), 1 for left and 2 for right; 3 is an error. Update header constants and literal modes. The default set also includes LF, CR, vertical tab and form feed; supply `" \t"` explicitly to retain the documented upstream set. Other upstream edge cases were not checked. |
| Array predicate | Calls it `pointerp`. [Reference][ld-pointerp]. | Rename calls to [`arrayp`](efun/arrayp.md), or provide `int pointerp(mixed value) { return arrayp(value); }` as a simul-efun. |
| Reference arguments | `&x` passes a reference without a special callee declaration; indexed lvalues and ranges can be referenced. [Reference][ld-refs]. | Both parameter and argument use `ref`. Only variables can be explicit reference arguments; cross-object and function-pointer calls cannot carry them. This can require interface changes. [Reference](lpc/references.md). |
| Byte values | `bytes` supports byte-string literals such as `b"abc"`. [Types][ld-types]. | There is no LPC bytes literal; values come from file reads, conversions or existing bytes. Bytes are immutable. [Types](lpc/types.md), [`to_bytes`](efun/to_bytes.md). |
| Regular expressions | Traditional and optional PCRE engines are selectable, with engine-specific option flags. [Reference][ld-regex]. | Patterns use Rust `regex`, without look-around or back-references. Numeric flags select filtering/index output, not an engine. Patterns and flags need separate review. [Reference](efun/regexp.md). |
| `terminal_colour(text, 0)` | Leaves colour markup uninterpreted while optionally wrapping the text. [Reference][ld-colour]. | Strips colour tokens. Code using `0` solely to wrap text has different output; use [`break_string`](efun/break_string.md) for ordinary text wrapping. [Reference](efun/terminal_colour.md). |
| `save_object` result and forms | File form returns `0` on success; a no-file form returns serialised data, with optional format selection. [Reference][ld-save]. | Requires a path and returns that path. No format argument or no-file form; callers testing the result as an error flag need changes. [Reference](efun/save_object.md). |

### FluffOS

Native classes support shared header identities, inherited definitions, named
construction, and member reads and writes. Every field replacement checks its
declared type; scalar classes retain nominal identity at runtime. Mixed member
access requires the actual class definition to be visible to the executing code.
Field views reuse storage by name and declared type across compiled definitions.
[`copy_class`](efun/copy_class.md) preserves all retained views in a shallow copy;
[`classp`](efun/classp.md) tests instance kind without requiring a visible
definition. [Native persistence](save-format.md#class-records) preserves nominal
identity and all materialized field views without loading class source files.
Repeated occurrences restore independently. General reflection and foreign class
save import still require further driver support. See [class support](lpc/classes.md).

| Topic | FluffOS behaviour | lpc-rs behaviour and porting impact |
|---|---|---|
| Random selection helpers | `random(n)` selects an index below a positive bound and returns zero for a zero bound. Empty array indexing errors; string indexing at the final boundary returns integer zero. String positions are graphemes: the reviewed index helper can return only the first codepoint of a short multi-scalar cluster, while longer clusters can error. [Random][fl-random], [length][fl-grapheme-length], [indexing][fl-string-read], [UTF-8 helper][fl-string-read-scalar]. | Lima's `choice` can remain an LPC helper using predicates, [`random`](efun/random.md), [`keys`](efun/keys.md) and [indexing](lpc/indexing.md). Return array elements or mapping values with their existing identities; select mappings by entry, including repeated equal values. String input returns an integer Unicode scalar, with combining marks and joiners occupying separate positions. Preserve zero for an empty string and errors for empty arrays/maps. Guard legitimately empty lists before selecting: testing the result afterward cannot handle an indexing error. Recheck lists after actions that may change them, such as sweep's first hit. |
| Array shuffling | `shuffle` reorders its argument in place, returns that same array, and leaves arrays shorter than two elements unchanged. Aliases observe the new order; element references are preserved. Requires `PACKAGE_CONTRIB`. [Reference][fl-shuffle], [implementation][fl-shuffle-source]. | There is no native `shuffle`; an LPC Fisher–Yates helper can use [`random`](efun/random.md) and array element assignments while preserving identity and aliases. A weighted selector such as Lima's `element_of_weighted` can omit its shuffle: for nonnegative integer weights with a positive, nonoverflowing total, each key still receives probability `weight / total`. A two-pass helper can total the weights and select with one draw, preserving the distribution while changing random-number consumption. Validate weights and overflow explicitly; choose the configured null result for empty/all-zero input. Native `random` rejects negative bounds, whereas the reviewed FluffOS entry point returns zero. [Source][fl-random]. |
| Regex association | `reg_assoc` returns parallel arrays of alternating gaps/matches and their labels. Earliest matches win, with pattern order breaking ties. Each search uses the remaining suffix; the default gap label is integer zero. `pcre_assoc` uses PCRE. [Reference][fl-reg-assoc], [core source][fl-reg-assoc-source], [PCRE source][fl-pcre-assoc]. | A mudlib simul can build the association arrays with [`regmatch`](efun/regmatch.md) and `RE_MATCH_SUBS`; there is no native association efun. Preserve empty gaps and advance empty matches by a Unicode scalar without dropping intervening text. Use an explicit `0` default label when callers require numeric zero. Searching a suffix retains the legacy anchor context; an offset into the original text preserves its anchors instead. Review patterns for the [native regex dialect](efun/regexp.md#dialect), scalar indexing and embedded NUL support. This does not supply full PCRE compatibility. The existing regex efuns share a bounded compiled-pattern cache per VM; frequent calls reuse resident patterns with the same compilation options. |
| Array and mapping predicates | `pointerp` tests arrays; `arrayp` is an alias. `mapp` tests mappings. Each returns integer `1` for its type and `0` otherwise. [Declarations][fl-core-spec], [implementations][fl-type-predicates]. | Use [`arrayp`](efun/arrayp.md) and [`mappingp`](efun/mappingp.md). Rename `pointerp` and `mapp` calls or provide simul wrappers. These predicates test container type, independently of whether the container is empty. |

[Ranges][fl-ranges], [indices][fl-indexing]. | Supports `<n` for arrays, strings and bytes while retaining native negative indices and bounds. Positions count Unicode scalars; bounds follow native negative/reverse indexing and strict write validation. Results preserve NUL and are limited to 8,192 UTF-8 bytes. Review grapheme/byte assumptions and size limits; upstream empty/insertion edge equivalence is unchecked. Compound string writes remain unsupported. [Reference](lpc/indexing.md#string-slice-assignment). |

Replacement rejects NUL and invalid UTF-8 code points. [Lvalues][fl-string-index-lvalue], [replacement][fl-string-index-replacement]. | Plain `text[i] = scalar` replaces one Unicode scalar and rebinds the captured owner, preserving old string references. Accepts ordinary negative/reverse indices and integer scalars including NUL, with strict bounds and an 8,192-byte result limit. Review grapheme assumptions, NUL handling and size limits. Compound writes, stepping, element references and output arguments need adaptation. [Reference](lpc/indexing.md#string-element-assignment). |

[Implementation][fl-strsrch-source], [Unicode helper][fl-string-search], [tests][fl-strsrch-tests]. | The native name is `strindex`; rename calls or provide a mudlib wrapper. [Wrapper][fl-trim], [helper][fl-trim-helper]. | Use [`trim(text, where, chars)`](efun/trim.md): 0/default for both, 1 for left and 2 for right. Move custom sets to argument three. #### Lima port configuration

The Lima port targets **`LPC_NULL_MODE=distinct`** with
**`LPC_CALL_OUT_PRESERVE_PLAYER=true`**. Its adaptations and active
validation use that configuration only. Earlier local runs also exercised
zero mode; those results are historical evidence, not a Lima compatibility
requirement. The driver supports both settings for different mudlibs, with
separate native tests for each. Distinct nil does not emulate FluffOS
`undefinedp` metadata; mapping membership and omitted arguments still need
the adaptations described below.

#### Lima port readiness

**The overall Lima port remains in progress.** Configured startup and shipped
tests are qualified milestones. The [collection helper update](#lima-contributed-collections)
records the current source inventory and outstanding consumer count.

As of **19 October 2026**, the active port is the dedicated `lima-lpc-rs`
checkout on `lpc-rs-port`, paired with native branch `lima-support`. Source and
qualification notes are committed through Lima **8a26d8c7** and native **ded2bc3a**.
The checkout's `README.lpc-rs.md` provides startup and test instructions.

The rebuilt release driver passes the configured fresh-account lifecycle,
native saves, fresh-process restart and saved login, with **151 clean preloads
per boot**. All five shipped test commands pass separately, followed by
`unittest all` and `unittest all quiet` at **59/59**, with **zero manual loads**.
See the [release lifecycle qualification](#lima-release-lifecycle-qualification).
The original prepared run loaded 42 programs individually. Direct cold combined
execution has both passes and timeouts under the unchanged 4000ms deadline;
the later [compiler profile](#lima-cold-compilation-profile) also records passes.
See the
[cold command audit](#lima-cold-shipped-test-commands), original
[combined qualification](#lima-combined-shipped-test-suites) and
[source inventory](#lima-source-coverage) for their distinct scopes. Runtime

A separate [ordinary-player lifecycle audit](#lima-ordinary-player-lifecycle)
passes creation, player-shell commands, native saves and fresh-process password

Original-driver saved-data/password import, alternate build options, unselected
or optional sources and documented upstream defects retain separate decisions.
The source inventory is not a completion percentage or a missing-feature count.

#### Lima CGI helpers

Reviewed on **19 October 2026** against the pinned Lima [autodoc helper][lima-cgi-autodoc],
[mud information helper][lima-cgi-mudinfo] and [finger helper][lima-cgi-who]. The
source adaptations use the configured distinct-nil profile; no driver API change
is needed. The malformed block-string delimiters and spaced HTML closing tags
are present in the reviewed upstream autodoc source as well.

Use ordinary string literals and native bare callbacks for the documentation
indexes/tree, and nil for absent route parts. Supply explicit nil parameter
defaults for omitted GET queries and handle empty queries before indexing.
For mud information, use `mixed *`, native mapping `filter`, and the size of an
array-based `regexp` result as its predicate. The finger CGI must supply all four
arguments required by Lima's colour wrapper and initialize an absent userid to
the empty string so the index route works.

The maintained Lima regression runner, `python3 tests/cgi/test_cgi.py`, compiles
the three actual helper sources and passes **55 LPC runtime assertions** in an
isolated copy. It checks documentation bodies/links, an actual inheritance tree,
mud-list sorting/filtering and Unicode, nil/empty queries, colour stripping,
optional finger fields, idle/mail formatting, and the HTTP form caller's two
arguments. Real class definitions, grammar, glob and ANSI translations remain;
controlled IMUD/finger records replace external data providers. This qualifies
helper output, without starting HTTP transport or testing live IMUD/account policy.

The full sweep immediately after the CGI adaptations measured **1008/1182 compile, 174 standalone
failures, zero regressions/timeouts/crashes**. Its three gains are the CGI helpers.
Of the remaining failures, 113 documented fragments have currently compiling
shipped hosts; **61 other consumers remain open for porting or explicit review**.
The sweep omits target constructors and retains source/profile hashes. It is
not a new lifecycle or live-service qualification.

member ranks and oldest-first listing. Result arrays remain independent while

The upstream sources were inspected; no upstream-driver execution is claimed.

The permanent Lima runner `python3 tests/collections/test_collections.py` compiles
both actual helpers and passes **37 LPC runtime assertions** in a temporary
library using the configured distinct-nil profile. Coverage includes partial/full
windows, repeated wraparound, capacity one, shallow-copy behavior, mixed values,
independent instances, zero-capacity behavior and stack depth after errors. The
fixture inherits the shipped helpers without replacement implementations.

The fresh full sweep measures **1010/1182 compile, 172 standalone failures,
zero regressions/timeouts/crashes**. Its only gains over the CGI inventory are

#### Lima contributed tar audit

Reviewed on **19 October 2026** at the pinned [tar source][lima-contrib-tar]. Its
`buffer` spelling is unsupported, but mutable bytes are unnecessary: a native
integer-array header can be converted with `to_bytes`, with payloads retained as
immutable bytes. A 2560-byte control archive using the source's basic GNU header
magic is accepted by Python tarfile 3.12.3 and GNU tar 1.35, preserving an exact
binary payload and an empty member. This was a separate feasibility control;
`contrib/tar.c` remained unported at this audit. Its later
[adoption](#lima-contributed-tar-writer) is qualified below.

The audit confirms a native `write_bytes` transaction-visibility bug: bounds and
negative offsets use physical metadata rather than the attempt's file view.
Writing after a pending creation returns zero; a second append is rejected after
`file_size` reports the pending growth. A negative offset after growth overwrites
the old disk-relative position, while pending truncation can wrongly permit a
write past the visible end. The [native correction below](#lima-transactional-byte-writes)
addresses this prerequisite; the writer still needs adaptation.

The utility also skips empty files, can index an empty work list after an empty
directory, omits terminating zero records and masks off full-record bytes at
16MiB. Replace string callbacks/argument passing with bound native functions,
create the output explicitly and bound large-file work across continuations.
Its existing 100-byte filename clipping and lack of archive extensions need an
explicit supported-format contract. The [GNU tar format][gnu-tar-basic-format]
and [Python close contract][python-tar-close] describe two finishing zero blocks;
GNU tar's permissive reader is not evidence that an unfinished writer is correct.

Thirteen isolated LPC controls record the observed write bug, binary/header
feasibility, arithmetic mask and callback binding/cancellation. They do not run
the original tar utility or qualify elapsed timer delivery. Library/profile and
native binaries were unchanged during the audit. Its source sweep was
**1010/1182** with 113 hosted fragments and **59 open consumers**; the audit
closed no source entry.

#### Lima transactional byte writes

Reviewed on **19 October 2026**. The native [`write_bytes`](efun/write_bytes.md)
now checks file kind and byte length after the calling attempt's pending effects
and the `valid_write` apply.
Pending creation, growth, truncation, removal and renaming therefore affect its
offset bounds; negative offsets use the pending end. An ordinary missing file
still returns zero. This corrects the driver issue exposed by the tar audit.

[`file_size`](efun/file_size.md) shares this metadata view. Text replacements,
appends and byte writes derive the size without copying their payloads or reading
the file, preserving write-only-file support. Character writes and renames fall
back to the existing content view. Permission applies retain their existing efun
names; `write_bytes` does not add a `valid_read` call.

Ten new byte-write regressions cover the pending operations, UTF-8 byte lengths,
permission-apply creation and write-only files. File-size tests also check pending
text appends without read permission and content-read errors during a rename.
All **29 byte-efun tests and 19 file-size tests pass**. The full workspace passes
**5188 tests**, with two ignored; all-target warning-free Clippy, formatting and
the ordinary optimized workspace build also pass.

Seven isolated controls using the real Lima simuls/includes and its unchanged
distinct-nil, preserved-player, 4000ms profile pass with the rebuilt release CLI.
They verify committed binary bytes, creation, repeated appends, negative offsets,
truncation and UTF-8 byte sizes. A five-write archive created in one task retains
its exact binary payload and empty member when read by Python tarfile and GNU tar.
The temporary master allows file access; this is a file-operation control, without
executing the tar utility or a gameplay/service run. Library/profile preservation
checks pass.

That driver correction did not adapt `contrib/tar.c`; its accompanying inventory
was **1010/1182**, with 113 hosted fragments and **59 open consumers**.

#### Lima contributed tar writer

Reviewed on **20 October 2026**, with native **29f120c2** and dedicated Lima
**e9a5cc59**. The actual `contrib/tar.c` now builds headers
in integer arrays, converts them with `to_bytes` and copies immutable payloads
with `read_bytes` / `write_bytes`. Explicit creation/truncation precedes bound
one-shot callbacks. Independent job state replaces the shared mutable header;
each callback queues at most ten entries or 1 MiB of payload, with a one-second
continuation delay. Empty files/directories, final zero records, archive exclusion
and the old 16MiB record-mask bug are corrected.

The existing basic GNU header and fixed mode/UID/GID/owner names remain. Member
paths are normalized relative to the mudlib root without a leading slash. Names
must fit 100 UTF-8 bytes, including a directory slash; overlong names fail instead
of clipping. The 11-octal-digit size field fits 8GiB minus one, a format limit
rather than a qualified operating size. There are no link, prefix or long-name
extensions. Inputs must stay stable, and callers coordinate jobs sharing an
output; asynchronous errors can leave a partial archive.

The permanent Lima runner `python3 tests/tar/test_tar.py` passes **21 LPC
assertions** and produces **six archives** through actual elapsed callbacks in
**16.54s**, using real simuls/includes and the unchanged distinct-nil,
preserved-player, 4000ms profile with a temporary permissive master. Python
tarfile and GNU tar accept the files and verify binary contents and metadata;
padding and both footer blocks are checked. Coverage includes empty roots,
hidden/nested entries, 1/511/512/513-byte boundaries, exact 100-byte ASCII/UTF-8
names, a source tree containing its output and a **16MiB + 513-byte** payload.
The large archive has **17 observed growths**; other jobs finish while it is
pending. This qualifies the helper, without a player command or full gameplay run.

The fresh full sweep measures **1011/1182 compile, 171 standalone failures**,
with **zero regressions, timeouts or crashes**. Its sole gain is `contrib/tar.c`.
All **113 hosted fragments** retain compiling shipped hosts; **58 other
consumers remain open**. Source/profile/compiler preservation checks pass.

At that qualification, native `read_bytes` materialized the whole source before
slicing each requested range, so the callback budget bounded queued payload
rather than read memory or I/O. The [range-read correction below](#lima-byte-range-reads)
addresses ordinary regular-file reads. Directory listings remain full `get_dir`
operations. No driver API was added for this port.

#### Lima byte-range reads

Reviewed on **20 October 2026**, after tar adoption at Lima **e9a5cc59** and native
notes **8fd4c59b**. Native [`read_bytes`](efun/read_bytes.md) now reads nonnegative
ranges of unchanged regular files in one blocking filesystem operation. A
supplied length bounds the read and allocation hint; an omitted length reads the
remaining tail. Metadata supplies only an allocation hint, not EOF bounds.
Authorization still precedes the path/view check, with no extra permission apply.
Negative starts, zero-length requests, pending target changes, nonregular inputs
and failed seeks retain the original content view. EOF still returns the
configured null value; zero length before EOF returns empty bytes.

Controlled native-API measurements use a **64MiB sparse input**, five fresh
release-CLI processes per case, identical validated data and a saved baseline
executable. Times include startup; RSS is the median process peak. These are
neither physical disk-throughput measurements nor whole-mudlib speedups.

| Request | Before (ms) | After (ms) | Before peak RSS (MiB) | After peak RSS (MiB) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 32 reads of 512 bytes | 970.2 | 11.0 | 87.1 | 22.8 |
| Whole file | 62.0 | 39.1 | 150.3 | 86.6 |
| 32MiB tail | 51.4 | 26.4 | 118.8 | 54.4 |
| Negative start, 512 bytes | 37.8 | 39.0 | 86.6 | 86.6 |
| Zero length | 38.6 | 37.9 | 86.6 | 86.6 |

The range workload uses a 512MiB address-space cap; whole-file comparisons use
1GiB for both versions. A separate **1GiB sparse-input control** reads at byte
1048576 under the **512MiB cap**, validates all 32 requested 512-byte results and
peaks near **23MiB RSS**. This qualifies bounded reads without loading the input.

#### Lima ranged weapons and ammunition

Reviewed **15 October 2026** at native **6f383ece** and dedicated Lima **e80b70e7**
with the source adaptations below pending commit. Distinct nil, preserved call-out
players and the 4,000 ms task budget remain configured. Original Lima **eefaff66**
is unchanged. This is native execution and pinned original-source review, with no
upstream driver execution claimed.

Ten Lima source files adapt the [ranged definition][lima-ranged-definition],
[ammunition][lima-ammunition-definition], seven examples and the
[fire verb][lima-fire-verb]. The collector is explicit `string *ft...` and retains
flattening; its default list is `({"single"})`, matching the default mode. A
protected base-description helper preserves parameterless `short()` and the
[plasma magazine][lima-plasma-ammunition] prefix. Two absent-object sentinels use
`nil`, and seven value arguments use float expressions. These retain the existing
[collector rules](lpc/variadic_parameters.md) and inherited-signature policy.

Live checks exposed callback sites hidden by the initial compilation failures.
Fire uses bare function values; ammunition schedules
`call_out(&finish_discharge(target), 0)`, binding the target in the callback.
When invoked, native [`(: name :)`](lpc/function_type.md) returns the named
function value without calling it. [`call_out`](efun/call_out.md) takes its
function, delay and optional repeat; callback arguments belong in the bound
function value.
The original fire verb also lacks its registered plural action and an indirect
living-target permission hook. A plural `handle_obs` adapter invokes the singular
action; an owner fallback reuses the target's existing kill-permission check.
Target-specific indirect firing hooks retain precedence. No native API changed.

**36/36 bounded targets compile**: the 11 family targets, all 17 tracked core
objects and eight related parents/commands. The whole-source inventory above
remains the earlier 818/1,180 measurement; it has not been rerun. Both original
source headers and LF/CRLF conventions are retained. CLI limits remain two
processes, two Tokio workers each, 4 GiB and 40 seconds per file.

The final production-driver run passes **30 lifecycle checkpoints**, two clean
**151-preload** boots and saved login, with normal exits. All **482** retained
first-session command records remain, plus **114** ranged inputs (596 total).
Nine real clones verify descriptions, four clip charge/max counts and numeric
values. Normal handlers cover single/semi mode changes, unsupported-mode refusal,
unloaded and unwielded refusals, matching 11mm/13mm loading, ready/unready, loaded
inspection, **15 shots**, both clip depletions and removal, reload and the next
shot. A separate call to the real quarrel `discharge` verifies its deferred move
to the target's room and clearing its weapon link to nil, proving target binding;
it does not qualify the crossbow's ammunition configuration. The actual flea's
maximum health is raised through its public API to survive the shots. Acceptance
uses normal handlers, with no new test fixture source or master grant. The same
six prior fixture sources, fixed local router packets and two address-only
overrides remain.

The default crossbow/quarrel identifiers and charge maximum, continuous combat,
AI equipment choice, burst-rate semantics and other gameplay remain separate.
Existing wear/wield and TCP work is not reopened. Native workspace tests were not
rerun for this LPC-only change. Evidence: /tmp/lima-ranged-ammunition-20261015.

#### Lima snapshot and GC timeout audit

Reviewed after mailbox commits Lima **4c15b53b** and native **8561a764**. Two
paused-clock tests reproduce the native mechanism independently of machine load:
a queued snapshot can exhaust the execution allowance before evaluation starts,
and a partial wait leaves only the remainder for evaluation. A late cancelled
reply releases its snapshot pin. Snapshot acquisition and atomic GC share the
committer, matching the observed callback timeout/cancelled reply around GC.
The actual replay's GC service duration was not instrumented, so its precise
pause cause and cost remain unisolated. No production GC/accounting change is made.
The [native diagnostics](transaction-diagnostics.md) now explain this case.

A bounded scalar-world fixture at 2.3 million cells/1,000 survivors measured
2.83s for current GC versus 1.62s for a reconstruction experiment in debug. An
optimized persistent-map sweep microbenchmark measured medians 617ms/310ms for
mostly-dead data, but 760ms/2,106ms for mostly-live data. These are separate
fixtures, not a measured Lima speedup. The optimized whole-crate test build was
killed before measurements; only the explicitly scoped map benchmark produced
optimized results. Temporary profiling code is not part of the shared change.

Recommend preserving the existing wall-clock allowance and atomic/quiescent GC
contract while investigating a selective reconstruction path for garbage-heavy
sweeps, with actual GC pause/occupancy measurements to choose its threshold.
Unconditional reconstruction regressed the map fixture; simply increasing Lima's
limit or disabling GC would leave the collector cost unexplained. Full Lima

#### Lima GC parallelism investigation

After commits native **50643c28** and Lima **e63c1f2a**, temporary instrumentation
separates survivor-map construction from old-map destruction. Both debug and
optimized native runs use the same **596-command prefix**, six fixtures, two
address-only overrides and ordinary five-minute GC period, retaining distinct nil,
preserved player and **4,000 ms**. Each retains **15,264 cells** from approximately
**899,000**: debug measures **21.320 ms** construction, **735.378 ms** destruction
and **885.167 ms** collector service; release measures **5.733 ms**, **235.220 ms**
and **267.665 ms** respectively. These are measurement runs, not new full replay
qualification or universal latency bounds. Destruction accounts for about **98%**
of the optimized rebuild phase.

A separate optimized imbl **7.0.2**/Rayon **1.12.0** study uses two workers, fixed
hash seeds, five rotated repetitions and the native allocator version. For a
2.3-million-entry map with Arc payloads, serial rebuild/destruction has a median
**200 ms** total; `par_bridge` takes **701 ms**, and buffering entries for parallel
disposal takes **249 ms**. The bridge serializes iterator advancement, while
buffering includes a full traversal before parallel disposal. imbl's existing
[Rayon feature][imbl-rayon-feature] covers `Vector`, not `HashMap`;
[Rayon's bridge documentation][rayon-parallel-bridge] explains its serial cursor.

An isolated local imbl API prototype instead exposes owned root branches for
disposal, preserving shared roots and the existing map layout. On the same map
layout, a second study measures **197 ms** serial versus **114 ms** using two
Rayon workers. Ownership probes cover empty maps, retained values, shared roots,
shared descendants and hash collisions. This API is not in published imbl 7.0.2
and is not integrated into the driver; the fixture is not a measured native
speedup. It suggests a narrower direction than partitioning all world storage.

Recommend a bounded native prototype of owned-branch disposal, with dependency API
support and normal transaction/GC checks before adoption. Workers must finish
inside the existing atomic collection; no background lifetime deferral is selected.
Temporary timing code is removed and production debug/release binaries rebuilt.
Driver storage, dependencies, GC/deadline/mode contracts and Lima source remain
unchanged. The prior **2,159 + 10** full replay remains qualification. Evidence:
/tmp/lpc-gc-parallel-20261017.

#### Lima native GC worker testing

The follow-up uses a detached native checkout at **d2a2c28b**, with the local imbl
owned-branch API and Rayon **1.12.0**. Production Rust code, dependencies and Lima
source/configuration remain unchanged. Only retired-map disposal uses workers;
tracing and survivor construction keep their existing paths. A lazy two-worker
pool handles large maps, with serial disposal for small maps or worker creation
failure. All work finishes before the atomic GC message replies.

The isolated prototype passes **5,134 workspace tests / 2 skips**, including five
new tests for small/serial pool laziness, shared snapshots, worker completion and
native array payload destruction before the GC reply. The **10 doctests**,
warning-free workspace/all-targets Clippy and documentation checks, formatting and
optimized workspace build also pass.

One paired optimized measurement uses the same driver binary, retained
**596-command prefix**, six fixtures, two address-only overrides and ordinary
five-minute collection period. A private prototype control selects serial or
two-worker disposal; Lima stays distinct nil/preserved player/**4,000 ms**. Both
runs retain **15,264 cells** from approximately **899,000**, with identical root
and marked-cell counts. Serial disposal/collector service measure
**275.136/315.667 ms**; parallel disposal of **32 owned branches** measures
**143.752/184.006 ms**. Collector service is **41.7% shorter** in this pair;
retired-map populations differ by **0.04%**. This is a native measurement, not a
full replay qualification or universal latency bound.

Existing transaction workloads run with one/two workers, fixed matched call
counts and alternating executable order. Both builds use the patched dependency;
the baseline keeps serial GC and the prototype adds native disposal integration.
Initial short samples show large
differences that do not persist in nine longer paired repetitions of the affected
cases. Repeated median changes range from **8.2% faster to 2.5% slower**, with
overlapping ranges; this does not establish zero overhead. All **362 measured
trials** complete their expected transactions without reply failures.

The results support owned-branch disposal without changing world storage or
deferring reclamation. Adoption still needs a maintained dependency API strategy;
the unpublished imbl extension and temporary path/control are confined to the
isolated checkout. The execution overview and native GC/deadline contracts remain
accurate. The prior **2,159 + 10** full replay and **966/1182** source inventory
retain their measured scope. Evidence: /tmp/lpc-gc-native-20261017.

#### Lima GC cleanup using published APIs

The follow-up source review and optimized container studies use the unmodified
registry imbl **7.0.2** archive, Rayon **1.12.0** and the native allocator version.
They compare serial cleanup, batched consuming iteration, payload extraction,
mutable-iterator pipelines, partially consumed map copies and fixed groups of
two/four/eight maps. A separate comparison selects standard or triomphe pointers
through public generic types while preserving imbl's default backend. All **700
measured trials** complete their survivor/content checks. Maps are constructed
independently; five rotated repetitions share one hash seed within each process.
Survivor construction and all disposal preparation are charged to collection.

Fixed storage partitions provide owned maps that Rayon can destroy using existing
APIs. With 32-byte values owning separate Arc payloads, two maps measure
**68.777 -> 37.526 ms** at **900,000 entries**, and **276.922 -> 152.490 ms** at
**2.3 million entries**, compared with a single serial map. These combined layout
and parallelism gains are about **45%**; two-map serial controls measure
**57.116/239.265 ms**. Four maps improve some large collections further, but do
not consistently beat two across sizes and access patterns.

Separate container benchmarks include snapshot clone/drop, reads and updates.
For two maps, clone/drop rises from approximately **13 ns to 24–25 ns**; sampled
read/update medians improve by **1–14%**. The read ranges overlap, and these are
container costs rather than interpreter transaction throughput. Batched iteration
has inconsistent owned-payload gains and substantially regresses scalar cleanup.
Mutable pipelines and the alternate pointer backend do not supply a convincing
general improvement. The published `OrdMap::split` implementation rebuilds entries
rather than detaching tree branches cheaply.

Recommend a bounded native prototype containing two persistent maps in the same
snapshot, under the existing single version and committer. Workers must finish
inside the accepted atomic GC message; quiescence and deadline accounting remain.
No fork or vendoring is required for this direction. The uncommitted dependency
extension proposal is withdrawn and preserved in its prior evidence bundle; the
active native checkout uses the original registry dependency and passes the
workspace build. No native storage change or new Lima replay is claimed. The
execution overview, earlier full replay and source inventory retain their scope.
Evidence: /tmp/lpc-gc-public-api-20261017.

An additional matched container study compares the patched branch API with public
map partitions in one executable: identical 32-byte values, survivor IDs, hash
seed, allocator and two workers. Seven rotations put each method in each order
position once; all **196 measured trials** pass. Owned-payload total medians are
**33.360 ms** for patched branches versus **26.898 ms** for two maps at **900k**
entries, and **123.999 versus 125.744 ms** at **2.3m**. The latter difference is
small relative to the overlapping ranges. Scalar medians are **13.570/8.132 ms**
and **61.529/59.062 ms** respectively. Four-map disposal reaches **78.776 ms** in
the larger owned case, with the previously measured additional handle-copy cost.
The partition algorithm uses only the unchanged public map operations; the local
extension is linked into both cases to hold the dependency build constant. These
are container measurements; native snapshot/transaction/GC validation is recorded
below. Main native source and registry dependencies are unchanged. Evidence:
/tmp/lpc-gc-matched-20261017.

#### Native validation of public map partitions

The isolated native prototype stores two or four ordinary registry imbl maps in
one snapshot, under the existing version and committer. A lazy two-worker Rayon
pool destroys retired maps synchronously inside the accepted GC message; small
worlds and worker-creation failures use synchronous serial cleanup. Quiescence,
deadline accounting and the production configuration remain unchanged.

Optimized native measurements use the same **596-command** Lima prefix, six
fixtures, two address-only overrides and normal **300-second** collection period:

| Native variant | Total GC pause | Retired-map disposal |
|---|---:|---:|
| Unchanged registry driver | 263.9 ms | Not separately instrumented |
| Patched imbl branch API, two workers | 169.4 ms | 132.6 ms |
| Two public maps, two workers | 178.2 ms | 139.9 ms |
| Four public maps, two workers | 193.1 ms | 144.0 ms |

All runs pass, collecting roughly **899k cells to 15.3k**, with **656 roots**.
These are single collection samples, not identical heap snapshots: retained
counts are **15,268** for the control and **15,264** for the other variants.
Two maps reduce the observed pause by **32.5%** versus the control and finish
about **5.2%** behind the patched reference. Four maps do not improve this case.

Both partition variants pass **5,138 tests / 2 skips**, including nine new
routing, snapshot, fallback and destruction-completion tests, plus doctests,
formatting, warning-free Clippy/docs and optimized workspace builds. All **560
transaction trials** and **96 longer repeats** pass. Longer repeats of the three
initially slower cases put two-map medians between **2.0% faster and 2.5% slower**
than the control, with overlapping ranges; zero overhead is not established.

The two-map implementation supplies a viable option using published APIs without
vendoring. That prototype remains isolated; its private four-map measurement
feature and auxiliary binary are not production features. Original public
debug/release executables were restored after the comparison. These are prefix/GC
measurements; the preceding full replay and inventory retain their scope.
Evidence: /tmp/lpc-gc-world-native-20261017.

#### Native GC worker integration

The production collector now uses the pinned owned-branch API when rebuilding a
large sparse world. A lazy two-worker Rayon pool finishes disposing of the retired
branches before the atomic GC operation replies. Small maps, unsplittable roots
and worker-creation failures use synchronous serial cleanup. The single world map,
snapshot version, reachability rules, protected identity cells, GC interval and
execution allowance accounting remain unchanged. No experimental worker switch or
partitioned storage is included. [Collector diagnostics](transaction-diagnostics.md#collector-diagnostics)
describe the threshold, worker lifetime and disposal timing fields.

The integrated implementation passes **5,142 workspace tests / 2 skips**, including
six new runtime tests for small/shared/direct cleanup, worker-creation fallback,
synchronous destruction and garbage-array destruction before the GC reply.
Doctests, formatting, warning-free Clippy/docs and debug/release workspace builds
pass. The first library-test compilation was killed before tests ran; its retry
with one Cargo job passed under the same resource limits, without a source change.

One optimized production run passes the retained **596 inputs** with **151 clean
preloads**, the same six fixtures and two address-only overrides. Lima remains
distinct nil/preserved player/**4,000 ms**, using its ordinary **300-second** GC
period. Collection reduces **898,442 cells to 15,264**, tracing **656 roots** and
**18,172 cell IDs**. Disposal of **32 owned chunks on two workers** takes
**154.114 ms**, with **201.341 ms** total collector service. These are single-run
measurements; the earlier timings above are historical samples, not a controlled
comparison with this run. No new full replay or source inventory is claimed.
Evidence: /tmp/lpc-gc-workers-20261017.

#### Lima basic player commands and help

The subsequent source batch, reviewed on **6 October 2026**, adds the protected
[dispatch adapters](#lima-command-dispatch-and-stdio) to `help`, `brief`, `verbose`
and `save`, preserving their private handlers. Their four sources now compile.
[Help command][lima-player-help], [brief][lima-player-brief],
[verbose][lima-player-verbose], [save][lima-player-save].

In the [help viewer][lima-help-viewer], use native callbacks and nil topic arrays,
search strings for directive colons and split formatter strings into line arrays
before paging. The [RST formatter][lima-rst-viewer] also needs nil for absent
header strings and released code arrays. In [HELP_D][lima-help-timers], remove
empty pathname segments before selecting directory names and use explicit
integer zero for absent restriction rows, retaining the existing comparison
expression and configured levels.

The seven-file adaptation passes nine compile checks and six ordinary-input
functional tests with real Lima master/simuls, user, human body and player shell.
Tests cover shared brief/verbose flags, saved flag restoration in new bodies,
plain/RST/Markdown help, multiple topic selection, missing topics and returning
to the shell. Workspace Clippy and formatting pass. Fixture access methods,
account setup, help index and topic files are excluded from adoption. Native code,
master policy and optional service settings remain unchanged. Full authentication,
help-index rebuilding, broader help applications and driver startup are not
repeated; the source inventory above remains its earlier snapshot.

#### Lima player status commands

The [HP command][lima-player-hp] and [score command][lima-player-score], reviewed
on **6 October 2026**, also need protected dispatch adapters while retaining
their private handlers. Score accepts parsed arrays or adapts the player shell's
raw text with Lima's existing option parser, including `score -t theme`. Use nil
for omitted argument slots and explicit numeric conversions for capacity
thresholds and the integer karma marker.

The [carrying-weight slider][lima-widgets] needs float values and float mapping
keys to match score's fractional capacity data. Two missing-name string returns
in [PARTY_D][lima-party-daemon], loaded by score, need nil. These four source
adaptations pass six compile checks and six ordinary-input functional tests with
the real Lima master/simuls, user, human body and player shell. Tests cover limb
ordering and changed health/intoxication, default score, experience, money,
karma, guild buffs, real party membership, report themes and fractional carrying
weight with widgets enabled and disabled. Workspace Clippy and formatting pass.
Fixture helpers, account setup and weight objects are excluded from adoption.
Wizard target selection, wizard-shell delivery, alternate combat configurations,
broader party workflows and full driver startup remain unchecked by this batch.
Native code and master policy remain unchanged.

bonuses without changing stored skill points. The equipment fixture follows the

budget. Workspace Clippy and formatting pass. Fixture helpers, items and account
setup are excluded from adoption. Wizard target selection, ranged weapons,
multi-limb coverage, alternate configurations, crafting operations and full
driver startup remain unchecked by this batch; native code and master stay
unchanged.

#### Lima version and timezone commands

The [version command][lima-player-version] and [timezone command][lima-player-timezone],
reviewed on **6 October 2026**, need protected dispatch adapters retaining
private handlers. Version uses existing native `__VERSION__` and configured
`__PORT__` values; Lima defines `__HOST__` itself in its configuration header.
Timezone must handle a bare query before numeric conversion and use zero as the
display fallback for an unset body timezone. The underlying value stays nil;
explicit zero and fractional offsets remain floats. Native conversion rules and
the body time module stay unchanged. Lima's existing `||` range condition does
not enforce its advertised bounds and is preserved by this port.

Eight compile checks and seven functional tests pass: six ordinary-input cases
cover version metadata, unset timezone queries, whole/fractional offsets, zero
and documented endpoints; an original-handler control reproduces the nil
conversion failure. Version's fixture uses a configured compiler port without
opening a listener. Workspace Clippy and formatting pass. Only these two command
sources change; fixture helpers, control command and account setup are excluded
from adoption. Full startup, actual listener metadata, login persistence, named
zones and invalid inputs remain unchecked by this batch; native code and master
stay unchanged.

#### Lima player time report

The [time command][lima-player-time], reviewed on **6 October 2026**, needs a
protected dispatch adapter retaining its private handler, an explicit long-format
argument to the mudlib time_to_string helper, and to_float before multiplying
integer body timezone hours by a float. Lima's [localtime header][lima-localtime-header]
expects a GMT offset at index 8; native [localtime](efun/localtime.md) returns a
nine-integer array with the daylight-saving flag there. The report parses the
existing [strftime](efun/strftime.md) `%z` result into signed hour/minute seconds
instead, without changing the shared header or native API.

The real [event daemon][lima-event-daemon] and its daemon-data base need no source
changes for the game-time report with the existing configuration and no saved
event registrations. Ten compile checks and five ordinary-input tests pass through
real Lima user/body/shell/frame objects: unset timezone, positive and negative
fractional hours, explicit zero and an integer body offset. A fixed nonzero test
server zone establishes the local/GMT difference against current wall time;
the tests also check game-time/weekday output, reboot/uptime text, unchanged body
values and return to the shell. Workspace Clippy and formatting pass. Only time.c
changes; the wider test viewport, fixture helpers and test server zone are excluded
from adoption.

Lima's existing player-time formula adds the saved offset to the server local
clock, although its prose describes GMT. Its fixed frame labels also remain when
an unset timezone omits the player date row. These source behaviors are preserved.
Full startup, scheduled event execution, daylight-saving transitions, alternate
game-time settings, display combinations and login persistence remain unchecked
by this batch; native code, master and the game-time configuration stay unchanged.

with `if (wielded_by)` and `if (!wielded_by)` instead of comparing the unset

T_STRING as a string; native [`typeof`](efun/typeof.md) returns an integer tag.
The old check misses parser error strings and tries to call them as object paths.

leave the type header, limb bookkeeping, master policy and native

of assigning a float product through `*=` to an integer. The reviewed
[FluffOS compound multiplication][fluffos-loot-integer-scaling] assigns that
product back to its integer storage, truncating these finite counts toward zero.
This preservation of count behavior is an inference from pinned source, without
upstream execution; native integer assignment remains strict.

The [coin object][lima-coins] overrides an inherited zero-argument `get()`, so
translate its two required parameters into `get(mixed args...)` and extract the
optional amount/type with nil defaults. Use explicit floats for integer amounts
passed to `split_coins`, supply the omitted nil argument to the existing
`format_list` helper, and use bare `long_descr` as its description callback.
These are two mudlib source adaptations; native APIs, master policy, death order,
random loot policy and corpse setup remain unchanged.

combat slot. Ordinary `look at Bills corpse`, sword taking, coin description and

`Bills`; `lifeless corpse` also names the pre-existing adventurer corpse.

NPC death stops its own combat immediately; the surviving attacker retires its
timer on its next native pulse. The one-second removal callback destroys the NPC
while retaining the corpse. Mortal player death applies the stock score penalty,

this revision, so its existing Void fallback is exercised.

Both corpse registration callbacks run through native timers; the state daemon
retains one queued job. Three native state ticks decrement decay from three to
removal and emit the stock messages without a new runtime-log entry. Fixtures
make jobs due using public queue methods; real minute-long waits are not tested.
Setup, controlled damage and observations stay fixture-only, and virtual
Connections collect output without sockets.

#### Lima stock player armour commands

Reviewed **7 October 2026** against the pinned Lima revision, with USE_MASS,
distinct nil, preserved call-out players and the unchanged 4,000 ms task budget.
The existing limb health, armour and wielding selections remain enabled.

In the bulk [wear handler][lima-wear-command], use [`stringp(ob)`](efun/stringp.md)
instead of `typeof(ob) == T_STRING`. Lima's type header defines T_STRING as text,
while native typeof returns an integer tag. The untranslated second `wear all`
tries to load an already-worn rejection message as an object filename. The
predicate retains the handler's existing skip-string policy.

The [hook filter][lima-object-hooks] must retain constant values before inspecting
function owners: `!functionp($1) || objectp(function_info($1)["owner"])`.
Armour's existing prevent-drop hook is the string "You'll have to take it off
first."; native function_info accepts only functions. The original Lima
functionp bit test also keeps nonfunction hooks, so this corrects the earlier
owner-inspection translation. Evaluation, callback-owner pruning, hook order and
removal policy remain unchanged. The [scarf][lima-armour-scarf] also needs `1.0`
at its float value setter; that item is compile-checked here, without claiming
player execution of it.

Five ordinary-input checks pass with real users, human bodies, player shells,
the stock grotto and its existing [fullplate][lima-fullplate]. Single wear/remove,
`put on`/`take off`, inventory annotations and messages to an observer agree with
F_WORN and the body's records. Fullplate occupies the torso and covers both arms
and legs once; removal clears all five records. Bulk wear/remove with the carried
glowing sword and lantern skips nonwearables and already-worn rejection text.
Repeated single wear/remove also keeps flags and coverage consistent.

Ordinary dropping of worn armour returns the existing take-it-off message and
leaves it carried and worn. Removal permits drop; taking and wearing it again
restores the same coverage. The [equipment command][lima-player-equip] reports
empty equipment, the actual glowing sword and fullplate, one armour row with
"Full body", and the expected empty-armour/empty-equipment states after removal
and unwielding. Use `remove adamantine fullplate` when checking an already-removed
item; the bare one-word noun can select the verb's earlier bulletin-board rule.
No parser, wearable, limb-record or equipment-command change is needed.

Plain torch defaults to 600 fuel units at the existing one-minute interval.
Ordinary lighting contributes one unit to body/room light and one inventory
marker. Due updates consume one unit; extinguishing preserves fuel and stops
scheduling, relighting resumes it, and final burnout removes the torch and
restores light. Stock magic torch also starts with 600 units despite its
unlimited-fuel comment: its unconditional check_fuel bypasses the lighting guard
without configuring infinite decay. Include light.h, set INF_FUEL in setup and
remove that override to inherit the normal guard. The adapted magic torch keeps

relights with a valid source. Finite overrides still burn out and remove; zero
fuel refuses lighting. The finite checks select three/two units through existing
setters; they do not wait through 600 minutes.

String source filters accept a matching lit torch and reject an unlit torch or
wrong source ID. The stock function filter rejects ordinary flame and accepts
the room's attached blue flame, with normal with-source actions and light/queue
updates. Validation uses parser direct/indirect permission handlers;
light_object still discards the optional source argument, and the source module
does not inspect it. These success paths use existing driver APIs. One accepted
blue-flame command invokes its predicate four times; filters must tolerate
repeated validation.

Rejected two-object commands currently report "There is no X with Y here",
hiding specific unlit/wrong-flame messages. Direct observation confirms the

Review this native diagnostic selection separately; refusals remain effective.

room ambient light permits lighting; a carried lit torch then supplies visibility
until extinguished, after which relighting is refused. No vision policy changes.

#### Lima wizard treefor audit

Reviewed **15 October 2026**, after socketinfo commits Lima **9bba6c12** and
native **14b13eca**. The original treefor command lacks protected CMD dispatch
and returns an integer from void main. Temporary repairs make the command file
compile, but its generated `__TREE__{ ... }` program still fails. The parenthesized
form also fails. An entry-only repair would therefore overstate port support.

At reviewed FluffOS **44532e02**, the [lexer][fl-tree-lexer] recognizes `__TREE__`
only with `DEBUG`, and the [grammar][fl-tree-grammar] calls the debug-only
[tree generator][fl-tree-generator]. The reviewed [CMake path][fl-tree-build]
enables `DEBUG` for Debug builds. This produces nested arrays of compiler-specific
nodes and opcode names; it is a developer diagnostic, not source evaluation or
portable AST serialization. These are pinned source findings, not FluffOS execution.

Native Rust already provides parsed and semantically checked frontend trees.
The existing `TreePrinter` omits nil, class definitions/construction, member access,
compound member assignment, references, spreads and explicit capture markers.
Probes retain those nodes in the AST while showing their missing output. It also
prints literal newlines without escaping, builds one combined Rust string and discards
some visitor errors. A small input produces **18,792 bytes** of tree output.
Directly exposing the current printer would preserve these diagnostic gaps.

Recommend `string *syntax_tree(string name, string source)` for a complete LPC
translation unit: use the checked frontend with ordinary source identity,
include/inherit authorization, transaction-visible files, current simul efuns and
diagnostics. Render the root's frontend AST, including inherit declarations rather
than flattening parent bodies, without publishing an object or running initializers
or functions. Constant folding and frontend normalization remain visible; this is
not a reversible source representation. Complete node rendering, escape literals,
propagate errors and enforce output limits during rendering. Return diagnostic
lines with an explicitly unstable format, reusing the same formatter for host tools.
This is a proposed API; no native syntax-tree efun exists yet.

Then adapt treefor to wrap its input as a function in a wizard-home source identity,
print the returned lines and report errors without the EVAL file/object round trip.
Disassembly remains codefor's separate purpose. Seven compile controls have their
expected outcomes; fourteen Rust inputs run in parsed/checked forms, with three
expected syntax/semantic failures. Includes, folding, inheritance markers, omitted
nodes, output size and lack of execution are checked. Dedicated Lima sources remain
unchanged. No production-driver run or workspace build/test suite is repeated.
The adopted inventory stays **80/81 wizard**, **4/4 guild**, **93/93 supports**;
treefor remains unported. Evidence: /tmp/lima-treefor-audit-20261015.
