#### Lima admtool races and memory audit

Audited **15 October 2026**, after management commits Lima **91c530e2** and
native notes **9f6ff77c**. This is source/compile review, with no adopted LPC or
native implementation change. The remaining mudinfo category has two leaves.
The races report already uses native class fields and genuine expression callbacks;
its one named action needs the established bare-function adaptation. Its top-level
glob includes six race files, including the documentation template, and excludes
restricted/coder. All six definitions compile and their literal adjustment sums are
zero. Report execution and category navigation remain unqualified.

Memory inspection is a genuine native feature gap. Lima calls memory_info(object)
at exactly one site, sorts every loaded object by the result and describes rows as
an upper bound that ignores sharing. The category catalog eagerly loads every leaf
for its metadata, so the unresolved memory controller blocks normal entry to both
menus. Neither a hidden controller nor a placeholder result was introduced.
Temporary callback proposals compile **41/42 targets**; the sole failure remains
memory_info. The admtool set stays **33/34**, and earlier command/lifecycle counts
retain their existing scope. No cold boot or runtime suite is repeated for this audit.

At the pinned FluffOS revision, with core F_MEMORY_INFO enabled, the object result
includes the full program plus instance data/header, even for clones; its no-argument
form uses separate driver accounting. Source review only, no FluffOS execution.
[Implementation](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/fluffos/fluffos/2c27287500daf48a87a1f89d69a97d8b9603028d/src/packages/core/efuns_main.cc).
Native [allocator resident memory](efun/query_resident_memory.md) and
[diagnostic source storage](efun/source_cache_stats.md) measure different things.
[Global inspection](efun/variable_info.md) exposes values but cannot supply compiled
program or allocation sizes. Serialized length is not an object-memory measure.

Recommendation, not an implemented API: add a native object_memory_info(object)
returning object/program/data/total byte estimates, then use its total in Lima's
report. Count shared values once within a queried object, include the full program
for each object's row, handle cycles, read through the current transaction and
avoid following ordinary object references into the whole world. Cache immutable
program accounting and calculate mutable data when requested. The report must say
estimate rather than claiming a strict upper bound or memory freed on destruction.
A global driver total is separate work; the proposed name gives the new API an
explicit object scope. Exact accounting boundaries and field names need agreement
before implementation. Evidence: /tmp/lima-admtool-mudinfo-20261015.

#### Lima NPC-script trigger registration and recovery audit

Audited **14 October 2026** after committing file function actions as Lima
**eff8eb0e** and adoption notes as native **56320537**. Actual dedicated module,
trigger, action and state-daemon sources execute without replacement. Upstream
claims are source review at **eefaff66**, with port-only runtime checks; another
driver is not executed.

The [script engine][lima-npc-script] registers the following trigger before running
the preceding action. A synchronous message produced inside that action can match,
so moving registration until after the action would lose that message. The existing
match path schedules progression while the action's own path also schedules it:
the synchronous case leaves two next_step callbacks and one response callback.
The earlier first-step unarmed trigger and adjacent-trigger premature registration
are reproduced again.

The [trigger module][lima-npc-trigger] reports every accepted pattern match to
triggered. It does not identify which patterns belong to the active script. A
separate ordinary pattern therefore advances a script waiting for another trigger,
leaving the script's expected pattern registered.

Actual [state-daemon recovery][lima-state-daemon] invokes recover and clears active
script tracking. The fixture's recovery hook records the call. An armed pattern
remains, conversation remains disabled and stopped ambient actions are not resumed.
A later match of that stale pattern still advances the idle index and queues a
response. A response and progression callback queued before recovery also survive;
explicitly executing the actual response pointer runs its command after abort.
The [action module][lima-follow-actions] cancels responses on object removal, while
the script's recovery path does not perform that cleanup.

Starting another script retains earlier patterns and pending progression callbacks.
Repeated starts with different recovery deadlines retain all three queue entries;
an old pattern can advance the replacement before its first WAIT executes. These
gaps follow the reviewed existing Lima control flow. No new native support
requirement or engine change is established by this audit.

All **seven focused checks** pass: six runtime groups and **six complete positive
compile checks**, including Robert, with **six following registered pwd inputs**
and zero caught input errors. The actual heartbeat and selected private response
callbacks are invoked explicitly. Evidence: /tmp/lima-npc-trigger-audit-20261014.
Distinct nil, preserved call-out players and **4,000 ms** tasks remain. Workspace
library-test build and workspace/Rust 2024 formatting pass; the temporary include
is restored, both source checkouts remain clean and all 38 frozen adoption artifacts
remain intact. Broker timing, full startup and native full suites are not repeated.
Initial fixture/control errors were corrected by inheriting the real conversation
module and compiling complete hosts; successful runtime actions/assertions remain
unchanged, and the failed runs remain in the evidence package.

Recommendation: keep these engine issues as separate Lima follow-ups and continue
the port with the smartmobs command and its real smart-movement inspection surface.
An eventual engine fix needs explicit pattern ownership, one progression callback
and recovery/replacement cleanup while preserving synchronous message capture.

#### Native process resource usage

Reviewed **11 October 2026**, following CPU audit commit **ffedc2a2**;
the resource API is committed as **82be256d**.
[`rusage()`](efun/rusage.md) now exposes the full 16-field process resource
mapping through Nix 0.31.3's safe `getrusage(RUSAGE_SELF)` wrapper. CPU times
truncate to integer milliseconds; peak RSS is normalized to KiB, including
Apple's byte-valued result. Other counters retain the OS's reported values and
integral-memory units. Values saturate at LPC integer bounds. Failure or an
unsupported backend returns a fresh empty mapping, while unsupported individual
counters remain present in successful samples, typically with zero values.
[Backend source and units][nix-rusage-source].

Readings cover all driver-process threads and exclude children. Each call reads
the OS again, including transaction retries; only the returned mapping belongs
to the transaction. Compilation and other process work are included, and multiple
VMs share these counters. The efun takes no arguments, supports bare function
pointers, and is appended to the catalog without shifting existing efun indices.
No apply, master policy, nil mode or uptime semantics change.

Nine new inline tests and the existing efun-order test pass: resource-field
conversion and units, millisecond truncation, saturation, failed sampling,
actual process readings, CPU consumed by another thread, fresh mappings and
ordinary direct/pointer argument rules. Locked workspace build, warning-free
Clippy across all targets, formatting and warning-free workspace docs pass.
Twelve copied-Lima compile controls have their expected outcomes: CPU and status
compile with their proposed dispatchers and the native provider, while unchanged
commands still fail at the dispatcher; eight support targets remain green. One
actual CLI sample returns all 16 integer fields. Execution checks ran on Linux
x86_64; Apple unit conversion and other upstream behavior are source-reviewed,
with no Apple or cross-driver execution claimed.

The FluffOS comparison remains source-reviewed at
**44532e0228f34be2184c701a361df4079371b8b0**, core `F_RUSAGE` enabled;
its raw platform maxrss differs from the native normalized unit.
[Implementation][fl-rusage-audit-source]. The native backend is unavailable
on non-Unix targets or Redox, Fuchsia, Solaris and Haiku. Dedicated Lima source
and configuration are unchanged by this native addition. CPU adoption and its
actual-resource verification are recorded above. Status's output remains a
separate command audit.

#### Lima wizard CPU resource audit

Reviewed **11 October 2026**, after date/README were committed as Lima
**c0e8c318** and adoption notes as native **9d363ace**. Unchanged
[cpu][lima-wizard-cpu] needs the command dispatcher and a missing native
`rusage()` API, also consumed by [status][lima-wizard-resource-status]. Its numeric
expressions already compile when a resource provider is supplied; no arithmetic
type change is required.

The reviewed FluffOS core implementation at
**44532e0228f34be2184c701a361df4079371b8b0**, with `F_RUSAGE` enabled, reads
`RUSAGE_SELF` and returns 16 integer fields on success, or an empty mapping on
syscall failure. User/system CPU times are truncated to milliseconds; the other
resource fields, including maxrss, are forwarded from the platform. The fallback
zeroes unsupported counters but still returns the full mapping on success.
[Declaration][fl-rusage-audit-spec], [implementation][fl-rusage-audit-source],
[fallback][fl-rusage-audit-fallback]. This is pinned source review, without
FluffOS execution or OS resource sampling in lpc-rs.

The existing division by integer 1000 loses subsecond CPU time before assignment
to float. With controlled 250 ms user plus 250 ms system time over ten seconds,
the original expression prints 0.00%; changing only the divisor to 1000.0 prints
5.00%. Preserve that precision, cache uptime once, and report unavailable data
when uptime is zero or either CPU counter is absent. Native
[uptime](efun/uptime.md) counts whole monotonic seconds since VM creation;
process CPU counters have a different lifetime in embedded/multiple-VM use.
This calculation is an average over uptime, can exceed 100% with multiple cores,
and is not an instantaneous load measurement.

#### Lima exec_code cleanup audit

mismatches. The bare destruct in misc.c resolves to the native efun, carrying

upstream execution claim.

The existing API supports explicit replacement of a removed name. Keep exec.c,
source generation/writing/removal, optional includes, resident-object lifecycle,
[M_ACCESS][lima-access] and current permission checks. Compile_string additionally
runs its normal write/load authorization; no native API, privilege exception,
new temporary-name scheme or permission-policy change is needed. Generated
set_privilege(1) is reduced to the directory's permitted privilege: the ordinary
wizard fixture's object has porter privilege and porter protection, rather than privilege `1`.
The refusal is caused by defining-program provenance.

#### Lima array set matching audit

Audited **10 October 2026** against native **ba9851fc**, after the inspector
adaptation was committed as Lima **07a85de0**. Native array subtraction,
intersection and union all compare stored members with raw, type-sensitive
equality. A stored destroyed-object reference therefore fails to match the
selected null value or a different destroyed object, despite scalar equality
and member_array recognizing those matches. The mismatch occurs in the
destructing attempt, in a later attempt after committed removal, and with
expired weak references. Rebuilding an array from a destroyed object variable
also retains the reference.

For example, in Lima's distinct-nil configuration:

```c
object o = clone_object("/target");
mixed *a = ({ o });
destruct(o);
a[0] == nil;                  // 1
member_array(nil, a);          // 0
sizeof(a - ({ nil }));         // 1: the stored reference remains
sizeof(a & ({ nil }));         // 0
sizeof(a | ({ nil }));         // 2
```

Integer zero is a different selector in distinct mode. Numeric type-sensitive
[collection matching](lpc/comparisons.md#collection-matching) is intentional:
1 and 1.0 remain different set members even though scalar equality and
member_array match them. Replacing raw matching with eq_in would change that
contract. The recommended correction normalizes only destroyed object operands
to the configured null value for comparison in all three array set operators.
It retains identity matching, input order, duplicate rules, fresh outer results
and original operand contents, without changing raw Eq/Hash or grouping.
Liveness must be read through the transaction; the operators currently hold
TxnHandle::with, so nested acquisition through eq_in/is_dead_object would spin.

All **12 focused native audit cases** confirm the current behavior and controls,
including literal nil, distinct-mode zero, numeric boundaries, string/bytes
content, nested container/class/function identity, compound assignments, pending
and committed removal, rollback, old snapshots and read conflicts. These are
standalone native fixtures for the configurable driver; Lima remains distinct
nil. An initial incorrect expectation that rebuilding the array would normalize
its members is retained in the evidence. Workspace and fixture formatting pass;
the temporary native test hook is restored byte-for-byte. Native implementation,
CLI, dedicated library/README/config and original Lima remain unchanged.
Evidence: /tmp/lima-array-set-audit-20261010. Full-suite and complete Lima
inventory/boot results retain their prior scope; no upstream execution is claimed.

Retain the adopted inspector and ammunition objectp filters. A native matching
correction alone does not make stale-target unsnoop safe: the daemon still
calls get_dummy_object on the target after subtraction. That cleanup remains
separate mudlib work. Audit notes are committed as native **240f4fb4**; the
[correction above](#lima-array-set-matching-correction) records implementation
and validation. The example and results in this audit describe native ba9851fc.

#### Lima saved error frame support

Native support added **10 October 2026**, after the
[dbxframe audit](#lima-wizard-dbxframe-audit) was committed as **7c8775de**.
[`error_handler`](apply/master/error_handler.md) now receives optional `frames`
and `frames_omitted` keys for uncaught evaluation failures, including interrupted
active evaluation. Frames run from root to leaf and distinguish the defining
program, receiver and current source file. Arguments and locals carry names,
runtime types and rendered values; a named variadic collector appears among
locals, and implicit closure arguments use names such as `$1`.

Adapt consumers of the FluffOS `trace` field to this schema. Values are immutable
diagnostic strings, with quoted and escaped strings and nonrecursive summaries
for containers. They are not raw LPC values to feed to the original formatter.
The snapshot reads the failing transaction before rollback, including reference
and closure cells, and does not retain mutable graphs. Limits are 32 frames,
32 variables per frame, 256 bytes per rendered field and 65,536 rendered bytes
overall; omission counts and truncation flags describe shortened data.

Capture adds no live-frame storage or successful-instruction sampling; the
64-byte CallFrame layout is unchanged. Nested reporting mappings are minted
inside each handler attempt, so retries do not reuse discarded cells. Native
tests exercise rollback, GC, nested clone initialization, interrupted nested
evaluation, captured/reference values, cyclic containers, included source,
inherited receivers, shadowed locals and Unicode limits.

Two checks against the actual dedicated Lima master, user, simuls and shell pass:
the saved uncaught frames remain readable after GC and dbxwhere still displays
the diagnostic, while caught regexp/modal failures retain message-only history
and rearm input. These use in-memory connections in disposable fixtures, with
IMUD startup and HELP_D data controlled. Dedicated source/configuration is unchanged.
The dedicated Lima master already retains the full uncaught error mapping.
The caught-input recorder still saves only the message: `catch` results and
handler timing are unchanged. At this native adoption, the dbxframe command was
still unported; the [subsequent adaptation](#lima-wizard-dbxframe-adaptation)
reports unavailable frame data for caught records. This native change did not
advance the preceding 45/49 transitional command inventory or claim a full Lima boot.

#### Lima wizard dbxframe audit

Reviewed **10 October 2026** against dedicated Lima lpc-rs-port **60059159**
and native lima-support **5d68e337**, after the caught-input recorder was committed.
The pinned [command][lima-dbxframe-command] and [help examples][lima-dbx-help]
require saved frames, their current argument/local values, and nearby source.
This audit adopts no source patch or native API change.

Small command adaptations are insufficient: it needs the established protected
dispatch_main adapter, bytesp in place of bufferp, a bare return after out, and
an explicit query_error invocation inside unguarded. Its old comma closure
returns the requested account name; indexing trace in that string fails and the
adopted input recorder saves the new failure. Integer-plus-string formatting
works, but the float branch fails; to_string renders that value successfully.
The original formatter also lacks object/class handling. Source excerpts should
use the frame's source file rather than assuming its program owns the line;
avoid a zero-line read before line one, because native read_file's zero count
means the rest of the file. These are command/source issues separate from the
missing native frame data.

The reviewed [FluffOS trace builder][fl-dbxframe-trace] supplies root-to-current
mapping entries with function, program, object, file and line, plus argument/local
arrays where available. Values are copied by reference-counted assignment;
mutable containers are not deep snapshots. Zero-argument and synthetic frames
can omit value arrays. Core [dump_trace][fl-dbxframe-efun] returns these entries,
and the [runtime handler][fl-dbxwhere-errors] includes them in its trace field.
The reviewed mudlib error-handler option is enabled by default and in
[Lima's configuration][lima-dbx-error-config]. The separate trace-code option
controls instruction tracing and is not required by this structured builder.
These claims are pinned source review at FluffOS **44532e0228f34be2184c701a361df4079371b8b0**,
with no upstream execution test.

Native [error_handler](apply/master/error_handler.md) receives error, location,
object and a rendered diagnostic, without structured frames. Caught input records
retain the message after [catch](efun/catch.md) discards the failing frames.
After the small command adaptations, both real uncaught and caught records
produce "No such frame." The missing trace is not an empty saved stack.
Caller inspection or evaluating a new callback cannot recover the lost values;
debug("snapshot_stack") is a test-only facility and rejects production calls.

The compiler already retains parameter/local symbols and their locations.
Register packing gives named locals distinct slots and updates that metadata.
A retained failed Task exposes the expected scalar arguments and locals,
including an unused value, while its exported diagnostic contains only a text
stack. Captured and reference parameters use upvalue cells, so raw register
slicing is insufficient. Container contents and captured values must be read
from the failing transaction before it is discarded; ordinary references handed
to a fresh handler do not preserve those contents.

All **3 runtime cases / 9 registered inputs** pass, including legacy-callback
failure/recovery, usage and empty history, real uncaught/caught records, self/last
lookup, history retention, float formatting and named-register inspection.
All **9 compile controls** match, isolating dispatcher, predicate and void-return
failures and preserving complete master/user/dbxwhere compilation. User/body/
room/shell/directory/modal/input state stays stable and input is rearmed.
Actual Lima master, simuls and command stack run with in-memory connections;
IMUD startup is stubbed and HELP_D has controlled saved data. Native metadata
controls retain a Rust Task, not an LPC-accessible frame API.

Recommendation: design general structured error diagnostics with bounded rendered
argument/local values captured on failure, then adapt dbxframe to that contract.
Immutable diagnostic data avoids retaining mutable transaction graphs or adding
live-frame storage. Define frame ordering, variable names, missing values and
truncation before implementation, preserving the successful execution path and
the existing 64-byte CallFrame layout. Start with uncaught error reporting;
caught message records need an explicit unavailable-frame report until a separate
captured-error access contract is agreed. Keep catch results and handler timing
unchanged. No Lima-specific trace efun or fabricated empty trace is proposed.

Workspace warning-free locked all-target/all-feature Clippy and formatting pass.
Original Lima, all dedicated source/configuration and native implementation/CLI
are unchanged. The preceding 45/49 transitional inventory retains its scope;
this audit is not a full inventory, boot or workspace-suite rerun. Evidence and
temporary fixtures live in /tmp/lima-dbxframe-audit-20261010.

Adopted **9 October 2026** after committing the [codefor

[`disassemble`](efun/disassemble.md) exposes the transaction-visible program's
existing listing formatter as separate diagnostic lines. It includes inherited,
nonpublic, closure and initializer code, projects inherited global operands and

prints actual instruction lines through Lima's raw-message flags and destructs

not invoked; native compile_string authorization and initialization still apply.

#### Lima wizard loadall audit

Reviewed **9 October 2026** against pinned [loadall][lima-loadall-command],
[command rules][lima-update-rules], [CMD][lima-command-base] and the committed
[destruction wrapper](#lima-wizard-renew-port). The dedicated lpc-rs-port checkout
was clean at **4798ac87** at the audit baseline; renew notes were native
**3f09e109**. No proposal was adopted by that audit and no native API changed.

Protected dispatch makes the private handler available to the wizard shell.
Its original positional callbacks, value capture and zero subtraction remain:
the callbacks already compile, and the destruction wrapper safely ignores
missing or destroyed references. The proposal checks every load result because
native [load_object](efun/load_object.md) returns nil on compilation or
initialization failure. Without the check, the command can print success after
a failed load. The reviewed [FluffOS loader][fl-loadall-loader] can throw on
compilation errors; this is source review at **44532e02**, without upstream
execution. Missing-file paths can also return zero there, as its
[reference][fl-loadall-reference] describes, so the original command's unchecked
results are not solely a driver mismatch.

The proposal preserves removal of all existing prototypes before any loads,
sorted nonrecursive selection, self-source exclusion and old clone state.
Remove hooks that leave their target alive still run again through explicit
destruct. Failed loads stop later replacements; prior removals and successful
loads remain after the input layer catches the error, and command output stays
buffered. Matching directory names ending in .c remain part of source selection.
As in update, resident master/simul targets are rejected before any cleanup and
require queued recompilation. That preflight is reviewed and compiled; runtime
cases do not attempt to remove live resident system objects.

All **17 cases pass across 25 registered inputs** against the final proposal,
including three baseline/dispatch/unchecked-load controls. They cover prototype
and clone identity/state, ordering, nil/dead references, real container cleanup,
missing remove methods, cleanup errors and repeated hooks, compile/initializer
failures and retry, source removal, argument handling, empty directories,
relative/trailing paths, self-exclusion, output routes and shell/input context.
Fixtures use actual user/body/shell/command code, an in-memory connection and
stubbed IMUD transport. Distinct nil, preserved players and 4,000 ms tasks
remain. **19 compile checks** have their expected outcomes: the original command
fails on missing dispatch, while three adapted variants and 15 supporting
targets compile. Locked workspace all-target/all-feature Clippy and workspace/
fixture formatting pass. All 1,547 dedicated library files, README,
configuration, native implementation and CLI are unchanged; temporary test
entries are removed. Earlier compile inventories retain their scope.

The [loadall port](#lima-wizard-loadall-port) adopts the exact proposal after
committing this audit, retaining its assertions without a new driver facility.

#### Lima wizard renew port

Adopted **9 October 2026** after committing the [renew
audit](#lima-wizard-renew-audit) as native **548db9fd**. Renew.c, the destruction
simul and README are committed as **4798ac87** in the dedicated lpc-rs-port
checkout. No native implementation, apply or permission policy changed.

Renew adds protected command dispatch and a bare void return. Its existing
save/remove/update/reclone/restore/move order remains. The destruction wrapper
handles contents after cleanup hooks and before native retirement: children try
to move to the captured parent environment; children still inside are retired
recursively without another remove callback. Actual environment and liveness,
rather than the move return value, determine fallback. Inventory snapshots are
processed in batches, and children moved or retired by earlier callbacks are
skipped. A fresh batch processes grandchildren moved into the dying parent.
Native authorization still applies to every retirement; callback errors propagate.
Raw native destruct retains its original behavior.

All **23 cases pass across 54 registered inputs** on the adopted sources,
retaining every assertion from the final proposal run. Twenty-one cases use the
checkout command and wrapper unchanged; baseline command and minimal proposal
controls retain their earlier sources. The original 14 cases retain their save,
type, identity, state, errors, output and context checks. Nine added cases cover
nested reconstruction, old contents moving after hooks, refused/claimed-success
moves, false results after movement, recursive fallback, no destination,
callback self-removal, alternate destinations, callback error and retry,
remove-argument forwarding and save omissions. The shared wrapper also works
through ordinary remove and explicit destruct calls.

Moving original contents can leave them alongside restored copies, as in the
reviewed upstream policy; this port does not change that renewal behavior.
M_SAVE's direct placement still omits reconstructed container relations and
capacity accounting. Buffered update-helper output, early removal on later

original player; FluffOS's driver-origin callback and temporary restriction on
other destruction are not emulated. The Lima adaptation retains native callback and
authorization contracts.

#### Lima wizard renew audit

Reviewed **9 October 2026** against pinned [renew][lima-renew-command],
[command rules][lima-update-rules], [CMD][lima-command-base],
[save module][lima-save-module], [object removal][lima-renew-removal] and
[destruction wrapper][lima-overrides]. At the audit baseline, the dedicated
checkout was clean at **b41ce738** on lpc-rs-port; update notes were committed as
native **2066a6ba**. No renew proposal was adopted by that audit and no native API
changed. The checkout already
uses clone_object instead of upstream string-valued new; the remaining baseline
command code matches the pinned source.

The minimal proposal adds protected dispatch forwarding `main(arg)` and replaces
an integer return in its void handler with a bare return. Checkout renew is
undiscoverable through the actual wizard shell; dispatch alone exposes the return
type error. Leaf-clone renewal works with the committed update and M_SAVE:
registered values retain integer zero, distinct nil, nested mappings/arrays,
Unicode and embedded NUL, while unsaved state resets. Old prototype and selected
clone identities are removed, a new clone is placed in the original environment,
and sibling clones retain their state. Even unchanged source with an old
timestamp reloads: renew passes an extensionless name to `do_update(file, 3)`,
whose exact-file metadata check has no source result. The upstream comment says
inherits are excluded, but the code requests update's timestamp-recursive mode;
that helper can visit loaded ancestors.

**Contents handling needs adaptation before adoption.** Recursive M_SAVE restores
a new nested tree, while native destruction leaves the original direct child
live with no environment and its descendants still inside it. At the reviewed
[FluffOS source][fl-renew-contents-source], when `NO_ENVIRONMENT` is not defined,
destruction instead calls each child's `move(parent_environment)` and destroys
children that remain in the dying container. This is source review, not upstream
execution. Upstream renew can also retain old children that move successfully
alongside newly restored copies; duplication is not solely a native mismatch.
M_SAVE also uses direct `move_object` for reconstructed children, bypassing
container relations: the fixture's restored child has no relation and contributes
zero capacity. That placement pattern is present upstream and remains a separate
source limitation, rather than an additional compiler or efun requirement.

Caught failures retain source ordering. Missing source and save/remove failures
leave the original clone live. Recompile failure follows removal without a
replacement; failed clone construction retires its pending clone. Restore failure
or a changed registered field type leaves the replacement live and unplaced;
strict store_variable checking is retained. A nonthrowing move refusal is ignored
and likewise leaves a restored, unplaced clone. No extra nil-clone guard is
needed: native clone failures raise. Input remains usable after each error.

CMD buffers output: a successful renewal displays or routes renew's own
“Updating” line, while the direct update helper accumulates its message in its
own unflushed buffer. An exception bypasses renew's final flush too. These
existing output and failure policies are documented without repair. Redirects,
pipelines and ignored stdin are checked; wizard identity, body, room, current
directory/file and modal ownership remain unchanged.

All **14 cases pass across 36 registered inputs**, combining 13 expanded-run
successes and the corrected recursive case in a focused rerun. Initial output
expectations incorrectly assumed helper flushing; the revised checks inspect
both command buffers. The added relation check initially expected integer zero;
the declared string's missing result is nil, now checked explicitly. Command
sources and the other cases are unchanged. All **21 compilation checks** have
expected outcomes: the proposal, 13 complete supports and four fixture checks
succeed; baseline renew, dispatch-only renew and standalone partial CMD retain
their expected diagnostics. Locked workspace all-target/all-feature Clippy and
workspace/fixture formatting pass.

All 1,547 library files, README, configuration, native implementation, CLI and
original Lima are unchanged; temporary test entries are removed. Tests use actual
master/simuls/user/body/shell/command/input/object/container code, an in-memory
connection and stubbed IMUD transport. Distinct nil, preserved players and
4,000 ms tasks remain. Earlier inventories retain their scope; full gameplay,
foreign save import and upstream-driver execution are not established here.
Disposable evidence stays under /tmp; local holds notes only.

The [renew port](#lima-wizard-renew-port) adopts the contents handling after
validating ordinary movement and recursive fallback. The minimal proposal and
its orphaning control remain historical evidence.

#### Lima wizard update port

Adopted **9 October 2026** after committing the [update
audit](#lima-wizard-update-audit) as native **6fbf05f3**. Update.c and README
are committed as dedicated **b41ce738** on lpc-rs-port; the checkout is clean. The
command uses protected dispatch, a typed closure, a bare void return, explicit
nil-load checks and a private file/load-time helper. No native API changed.

Inherited programs are compiled as part of the child; inheritance alone does not
create parent objects. The command therefore reloads only loaded parent
prototypes: `-r` visits direct parents, and `-R` visits all ancestors in
compilation order, including loaded ancestors behind unloaded parents. `-z`
keeps recursive load-time propagation for loaded direct parents and checks the
remaining inherited source timestamps through
[deep_inherit_list](efun/deep_inherit_list.md). It never instantiates unloaded
fragments such as names.c. Missing inherited source timestamps raise an error
instead of being treated as unchanged. A loaded parent's same-second update can
still leave its child unchanged, as recorded in the audit; the adaptation
retains that source behavior.

All **34 cases pass across 68 registered inputs**: 32 in the full run and the
two corrected fixture cases in a focused rerun; all other cases and command
sources are unchanged. Twenty-nine cases use the adopted checkout source
unchanged; one appends a fixture clock, one records the first caught error, and
three controls retain original, unchecked and audited sources. The two
standard-library prototype reload cases seed Lima's existing mudlib role so that
the fixture wizard has the required write authority. Ordinary and recursive room
reloads return the connected player, and timestamp skips also return the player
to the retained room. A changed transitive names.c fragment is compiled into the
new room without loading that fragment as an object. Direct/recursive parent
identities, transitive timestamp changes, old clones, reset globals, remove
arguments, batches, errors, current-file defaults and redirects pass. Missing
source and invalid fragments retain the existing early cleanup and error
suppression: evacuated players remain in Void after failure. Resident
master/simul objects are refused before cleanup; master has its existing queued
command.

Fresh compilation reaches **32/49 transitional commands** and all **53 complete
supports** across **82 distinct checks**. Only update.c is newly successful,
with no regressions or timeouts. Locked workspace all-target/all-feature Clippy
and workspace/fixture formatting pass. The other 1,546 library files,
configuration, native implementation, CLI and original Lima are unchanged;
temporary test entries are removed. Fixtures use the actual user, body, shell,
input, command and room code with an in-memory connection and stubbed IMUD
transport. Distinct nil, preserved players and 4,000 ms tasks remain. Earlier
inventories retain their scope; upstream-driver execution, broad upgrades and
complex virtual objects are not established here.

Next: resolve the contents-handling mismatch in the [renew audit](#lima-wizard-renew-audit)
before adopting that command; loadall can follow.

#### Lima wizard update audit

Reviewed **9 October 2026** against pinned [update][lima-update-command],
[command rules][lima-update-rules], [CMD][lima-command-base],
[command parsing][lima-command-daemon], [destruction wrapper][lima-overrides]
and [master][lima-master]. The backup/restore port is committed as dedicated
**6cc443fb**, with native notes as **b4c47429**. Dedicated Lima is clean on
lpc-rs-port at this audit; update.c matched pinned upstream. The audit's
base proposal was not adopted until the inherited-module adaptation in the subsequent port.

The command needs protected dispatch forwarding arguments and flags, native
`(: [object ob] { ... } :)` closure syntax, and a bare return in its void main.
Its `-z` branch uses only file size, modification time and prototype load time
from stat. Pinned [FluffOS stat source][fl-update-stat-source] (F_STAT enabled)
returns those in its first three fields. A private helper can compose
[file_size](efun/file_size.md), [file_time](efun/file_time.md), find_object and
[object_time](efun/object_time.md); no new stat efun is needed. This is source
review and native execution, with no upstream-driver execution claim.

Retain synchronous destruct/load: the prototype's identity and globals are
replaced, create runs again, remove receives integer 1, and old clones keep their
old program and state. Queued [in-place recompilation](efun/request_object_recompile.md)
would change that contract. Resident master/simul objects cannot use this path;
the proposal refuses them before cleanup and directs master users to the existing
master command. Its public do_update also applies the check for direct callers.
The existing permission policy is unchanged.

Native [load_object](efun/load_object.md) returns nil on compile or initializer
failure. The unguarded control destroys the old prototype and falsely reports
"Updated and loaded." The proposal checks both load sites and raises an error
instead. Existing per-file catch in plural/glob handling still suppresses errors
and continues the batch. A default-current-file error reaches input handling and
leaves a usable shell; successful loads alone report success. Destruction retained
by a caught error is not restored, and players evacuated from a failed room reload
stay in Void. Successful room reload returns connected players and removes
unlinked contents through the existing closure.

All **25 cases pass across 50 registered inputs**: normal/unloaded/current-file
reloads, new identity and reset globals, old clones, direct and recursive inherit
prototype reloads, flag precedence, timestamp skips/updates, batch recovery,
compile and initializer errors, direct do_update, room occupants and output routes.
The first runtime run passed eighteen of nineteen cases. Its failed -z expectation
exposed the source's second-resolution edge: a changed parent's returned time can
equal a child's load time, leaving that child unchanged. The ordinary propagation
case now waits for a later second without removing any assertion; an additional
case controls only command time to prove the edge. Initial sources, logs and the
diff remain. Older cases gain inherited-code assertions, and five cases add the
clock edge, resident-object checks, initializer failures and inherited-room failure cleanup.
The expanded run passed 23/24; its room assertion conflated inherited-load failure
with a clean timestamp skip. That case now uses an explicitly broken parent source
and verifies its load error and prior cleanup in a passing focused rerun. Other
twenty-three cases, command source and helpers are unchanged. A separate
fixture records the original per-file catch to confirm the earlier deep-room
failure, with no source-parent edits: it cannot load /std/object/names.c.
A standalone compile confirms that [fragment][lima-update-names] lacks
pluralize and is_visible, supplied by its [full object][lima-update-baseobj]
through inheritance. The per-file catch suppresses this error after moving the
player to Void; the old room stays loaded. This port mismatch must be resolved
before ordinary room -z updates can work. The tested proposal needs an inherited-module
adaptation before adoption: do not instantiate unloaded inheritance fragments;
reload existing parent prototypes when requested, and inspect inherited source
timestamps for -z using the child's inheritance metadata.

Native compilation reads current inherited source even when parent prototypes
remain loaded. The default and -r/-R cases confirm this separately from which
prototype identities are destroyed; the command does not change compiler policy.
Other source behavior remains: -r updates direct parents, -R recurses, -z wins
over both, shell cwf is set before failure, and room contents are processed before
-z decides whether to skip reloading. A failed inherited load leaves the old
room live, unlinked contents removed and evacuated players in Void. Per-file
error suppression and early cleanup remain source policies; inherited-fragment
loading is the compatibility issue to resolve.

All **24 complete focused targets compile across 29 checks**, retaining parser,
void-return and missing-stat controls. An initial compile-runner expectation
omitted dispatch; corrected controls expose the actual later errors. Locked
workspace all-target/all-feature Clippy and workspace/fixture formatting pass.
The fixture uses one in-memory connection and actual master, simuls, user, human
body, shell, command/input, object and room code; IMUD transport is stubbed, with
recording helpers and small reload targets. Every input checks line mode, echo
and rearming. All 1,547 library files, README, configuration, native implementation,
CLI and original Lima remain unchanged; temporary entries are removed. Distinct
nil, preserved players and 4,000 ms tasks remain. Cargo uses two jobs and serial
tests, CLI checks at most two processes without overlap, disposables in /tmp and

#### Lima wizard backup and restore audit

Reviewed **9 October 2026** against pinned [bk][lima-backup-command],

bk and rst matched pinned upstream byte for byte. Its proposal was not adopted.

Both commands lack dispatch_main. Dispatch alone compiles bk but exposes rst's
`!sFileContents = read_file(...)` type error: the native parser negates the
assignment target. Explicit grouping compiles. That syntax control opens the
restore menu, but its comma callback never invokes prompt_user, so selecting a
backup changes nothing and retains the menu handler. Bound callbacks are needed
at all three initial, menu and retry sites.

Native [read_file](efun/read_file.md) and [write_file](efun/write_file.md)
raise for file failures. An uncaught-I/O control selects a backup deleted after
the menu opened; its read error reaches the user dispatcher and leaves the old
restore handler active. The disposable two-file proposal adds ordinary protected
dispatch, binds prompt_user with &prompt_user(asContents, sPath, sOrigFile),
and catches the existing read/write sites so their diagnostics and cleanup run.
The read assignment inside catch also removes the ambiguous negation. Native
writes succeed with 1 or raise, so their old false-result branches become catch
checks. No native API change is needed; existing path and naming logic remain.

All **eighteen scenarios pass across 64 registered inputs**. Fifteen proposal
cases use 55 inputs; baseline, comma-callback and I/O controls use nine.
The first run passed seventeen cases; the collision case failed because its
message assertion assumed an unwrapped line. Only that fixture assertion was
changed to normalize whitespace before the full rerun; the original run and
diff are retained.
Backup creates bak, preserves source bytes, formats the native calendar date,
adds the .c fallback and sets cwf. Empty files back up and restore correctly.
Relative cwf works. The timestamp-collision case alone appends a fixture clock
returning 1700000000: existing dated and timed backups remain, while the final
incremented-seconds fallback overwrites its preexisting file as the source does.
It uses real native localtime and file operations, without a real-time scheduling
or upstream-execution claim.

Restoration selects among sorted backups, replaces or recreates the target,
preserves backup bytes and sets the original literal cwf path. Menu redisplay
and repeated invalid selections retain binding through modal_simple; q and x
cancel. Empty input is invalid rather than cancellation, and `1junk` retains
the existing leading-integer selection. Deleted backups and directory destinations
report the original read/write messages, pop the handler and leave a usable
shell with unchanged file state. Initial buffered output follows outer redirects;
later restoration messages reach the connection. Context and input rearming pass.

Existing quirks stay separate from compatibility work: bk prepends pwd even when
cwf is absolute, so an absolute default can fail its read; its read-failure branch
continues and can create an empty bak directory before reporting write failure.
A relative subdirectory source lacks a corresponding backup subdirectory and
reports write failure. The final collision fallback can overwrite an older
backup. None of these algorithms or policies is repaired by this proposal.

retain their scope. Concurrent restoration, stack teardown, upstream-driver

#### Lima wizard command-path audit

Reviewed **9 October 2026** against pinned [addpath][lima-addpath-command],
[rmpath][lima-rmpath-command], [printpath][lima-printpath-command],
[command rules][lima-trans-command-rules], [wizard shell][lima-wizard-shell],

after committing du as dedicated **b1af8f57** and its port notes as native
**bb40d8a9**. The three commands are unchanged from upstream and lack CMD
dispatch. The disposable proposal adds protected dispatch calling main(arg)
for addpath/rmpath and main() for printpath. Native implode accepts a delimiter,
so replace the three callback-based calls with [reduce](efun/reduce.md),
retaining the callbacks and explicit initializers.

The pinned [FluffOS fold implementation][fl-path-fold] returns integer zero
for an empty array without an initializer, and returns a supplied initializer
unchanged. Native reduce returns nil for the first case in distinct-nil mode.
The proposal therefore handles empty printpath explicitly with integer zero;
nonempty paths still use the original left fold. Its empty report remains
`Your current path is: 0`. No native API or null-mode change is needed, and
no proposal is adopted. This is public source review and lpc-rs execution,
without upstream-driver execution or a FluffOS build.

The shell's saved path array and normalized lookup cache are distinct. Adding
a directory starts with the normalized cache and appends one trailing slash;
the variable hook normalizes the cache again, while persistence retains the
supplied array. Removing a directory saves the remaining normalized entries.
Duplicate additions and absent-member removals preserve both arrays. Root is
normalized to `/` while a new root entry is saved as `//`. The existing save
module and real shell reload restore the saved array and rebuild the cache.
Actual command selection follows path order immediately, including after a
removal, readdition, rehash and reload.

Existing source behavior remains separate: both addpath and rmpath require one
existing directory through Cmd_rules, despite addpath's optional-argument prose.
Removing the final entry prints `Your path is now` because the unchanged seeded
formatter slices off its last two characters. Printpath ignores extra arguments;
all three commands ignore incoming text. Absolute command paths and the shell's
resetpath binding still work when the search path is empty. These behaviors are
retained rather than repaired during compatibility work.

All **ten scenarios pass across 55 registered inputs**: eight proposal cases
use 48 inputs, the undiscoverable baseline uses four, and the unguarded empty-fold
control uses three, including recovery. Exact reports and both path arrays cover
empty/singleton/default paths, duplicate and absent members, directory-rule
refusals, relative/absolute/quoted/Unicode paths, single-match globbing and root.
Ordinary lookup order, saved payloads and actual shell reload pass. Pipelines,
overwrite/append redirection and ignored stdin pass. The expected empty-fold
control error and the proposal's output-limit refusal rearm input and permit
the next command; the latter preserves paths and sends no downstream partial
report. Real account/body/room/directory state and shell input-stack return are
checked through line-mode callbacks with echo and rearming.

fail the four required dispatch calls each; dispatch-only controls expose the

control assertion used the wrong diagnostic wording; only that assertion was

library files, README, configuration, native implementation, CLI and original

preceding 20/49 transitional and broader evidence retain their scope. Temporary

pat[i..++i]: evaluating the upper bound changes the lower bound's retained
variable register. An escaped pair loses its backslash, so a slash-containing

actual-module execution reproduce this; slice assignment already snapshots its
start operand. Fix slice-read operand preservation before adopting grep, then
require successful slash matching instead of the diagnostic failure assertion.

#### Lima IMUD networking audit

The [IMUD daemon][lima-imud-daemon], [OOB module][lima-imud-oob] and
[socket wrapper][lima-imud-socket] were reviewed on **5 October 2026** at the
listed Lima revision. IMUD uses outgoing TCP to its router, an OOB listener on
`__PORT__ + 1`, and outgoing OOB connections for mail/file transfers. These paths
all use MUD mode; an outgoing-only connector is insufficient. The wrapper's UDP
and subprocess branches are not used by these paths. Excluding optional
`external_start` support from a port adapter requires no subprocess efun.

FluffOS's socket implementation and value serializer were source-reviewed at
`44532e0228f34be2184c701a361df4079371b8b0`, with `PACKAGE_SOCKETS` relevant to
sockets and `PACKAGE_EXTERNAL` to subprocesses; IPv6 paths depend on `IPV6`.
No upstream build or execution was performed. MUD mode frames serialized values
with a four-byte network-order length, including the payload's terminal NUL.
Its write results distinguish rejected data from accepted, buffered data, and
release/acquire transfers ownership through a synchronous callback.
[Socket implementation][fl-network-sockets], [value serializer][fl-network-values],
[package signatures][fl-network-signatures], [subprocess implementation][fl-network-external].

The audit recommends a reusable native TCP service carrying
[`bytes`](lpc/types.md), with function callbacks, transactional ownership
and bounded output, and an explicit I3 codec in the mudlib. Native
[`save_value`](efun/save_value.md) has different nil, floating and string forms;
its output cannot be sent directly as an I3 packet. Preserve wire numeric zero
and normalize only nullable protocol fields before typed handler calls.

Socket operations must fit the driver's transaction model: physical IO follows
commit, so admitted bind/connect requests need asynchronous success/failure
events. Preserve per-socket commit order and stable input events across retries.
The logical ownership-transfer callback can run within the current transaction.
Callback context, draining, owner destruction, GC roots and master authorization
need explicit contracts before implementation; the existing interactive
[`write_socket`](efun/write_socket.md) does not provide general TCP sockets.

Compile-only controls also expose ordinary port changes in channel/user-cache
handlers, OOB timers and reply markers, and file metadata/callback reduction.
Later errors remain masked by the file-handler frontier. That audit adopted no
production patch and established no clean complete-daemon compile or transport
execution; the native API was implemented subsequently.

The subsequent TCP interface combines connect/listen setup and uses
one event callback for completion, accepted streams, raw reads, EOF and closure.
Writes admit a whole bytes buffer or refuse it without taking a prefix; the
driver handles partial OS writes. Accepted-stream reads pause during their
listener callback so ownership can be assigned synchronously. Socket commands
need ordered publication through the committer before independent task effect
delivery; physical IO remains outside the committer. The implemented contract is
documented in [TCP sockets](tcp-sockets.md).

The native bookkeeping foundation now provides transactional socket records,
owner inventories, count/output limits, whole-buffer write admission and
commit-ordered command batches. Destruction and failed initialization retire
owned records transactionally, and GC traces registered callback captures.
Retired handles disappear from inspection immediately while retaining their count
charge until queued commands, workers and pending descriptor handoffs are disposed;
retirement cannot bypass the bounds on buffered output by reusing quota early.
Native TCP workers resolve/connect or bind, finish partial
writes in order, drain graceful closes with a timeout, and interrupt retirement.
Readiness, raw input, EOF, accepted children, full-buffer completion and terminal
state publish through the native transaction runner. Transactional FIFO inboxes
retain immutable event payloads until acknowledgement commits; native leases reread
registration on each attempt. Input bytes and pending accepts have separate positive
limits. Pending accepts also reserve VM quota before the physical accept, including
one unpublished slot while a listener waits for a connection. Accepted-child reads
and queued writes stay paused until its listener event succeeds; failure or listener
close discards undelivered children. EOF preserves the write side, and repeated
output-empty transitions share one pending `drained` wakeup. Close and terminal
failure remove queued drained wakeups. Accepted descriptor handoff survives listener
close after successful notification, and activation checks both the scheduling owner
and the callback's owner/receiver. Deterministic native
and local loopback tests cover this layer. The native runtime
dispatches three-argument LPC callbacks serially per handle while allowing
other sockets to progress independently. Every attempt leases the same event with
the current owner and pointer; callback writes and acknowledgement commit together.
Uncaught errors abort callback writes, validate the failed attempt's reads, report
through the existing runtime-error path and discard only that registration's event.
An ownership change invalidates a stale error as well as a successful old callback.
Failed accepts retire undelivered children, and terminal errors still retire metadata;
an unresolvable pointer retires the socket. Entries use driver origin, no player or
command context, and the scheduling owner as caller even for another receiver.
Native pointer type checks, named-function rebinding and retained closure code apply.
The [eight TCP efuns](tcp-sockets.md) expose creation, whole-buffer writes, close,
inspection and synchronous ownership offers, gated by [valid_socket](apply/master/valid_socket.md).
Acquisition requires the named recipient's active offer call. Offers use efun origin
and native catch semantics: a caught error retains prior acquisition, while an
uncaught transaction abort discards it. The driver starts TCP before preloads and
stops it before closing the committer. Lima's bounded I3 codec, MUD-mode TCP
wrapper and tested IMUD router/OOB exchanges are adopted in the local Lima port.
Fresh full-overlay startup and saved-state IMUD/login checks pass; a separate RST
cleanup failure remains on restart.

#### Lima TCP wrapper and I3 adaptation

A further source review on **6 October 2026**, against the same pinned Lima and
FluffOS revisions, finds no additional transport efun required for the router/OOB
paths. Adapt MUD-mode connections/listeners to the native event callback, acquire
accepted children during the listener callback, and deliver `(wrapper, nil)` once
before the child's packets. Keep numeric wire zero unchanged; normalize only
nullable fields before calling typed protocol handlers.

Use bounded framing and an explicit value codec in the mudlib. Native
[`restore_value`](efun/restore_value.md) also has different string escape/newline
semantics and accepts native value forms that do not belong in I3. String and bytes
concatenation have an 8 KiB result limit; conversions can create larger values.
Use bounded fragments or preallocated byte arrays, and send larger frames through
admitted chunks. The native input/output queue budget is not an I3 frame limit.
The diagnostic codec supports a 256 KiB payload, including its terminating NUL,
64 container levels and 32,768 values. It preserves integer wire zero and encodes
native nil as zero. It rejects unsupported values, malformed or incomplete
payloads, duplicate wire keys and nonfinite floats. Floats use the reviewed
writer's six-decimal precision; distinct float keys that alias after formatting
are rejected. Framing extracts one packet at a time, retains unread input and
requires reset after a caught framing or decoding error.

Lima's wrapper closes and immediately destroys its owner. Native destruction
retires queued output, so keep a deliberately closing wrapper alive until its own
queue and native close finish. Actual destruction and driver shutdown still cancel
resources. Clear the daemon's logical reference when intentionally replacing a
router, and guard later callbacks by connection identity. Peer EOF needs explicit
translation to the I3 close path because the native write side stays open.
Catch malformed framing inside the event and commit cleanup: an uncaught callback
error rolls back the cursor while discarding that raw-input event.

The existing master signature compiles, but its wrapper grant must account for
new inspection operations and ownership recipients. Preserve the wrapper's outgoing
privilege check. The absent `send_telnet_nop` keepalive and swallowed outgoing-mail
send failures are existing Lima concerns for integration, not reasons to add native
Telnet framing or weaken queue bounds. Fresh distinct-nil probes and compile controls
support these adaptations.

The diagnostic codec passes compilation and 52 LPC case groups, including
source-derived golden frames, arbitrary fragmentation, coalescing, malformed
input, exact limits and large mudlist/file/mail-shaped packets. Four runtime
tests cover transaction rollback, committed failure/reset, concurrent cursors
and a maximum-size frame received across 33 committed input calls. All checks
use the unchanged four-second task budget; the runtime tests bootstrap the actual
Lima master/simuls. FluffOS is not executed.

The diagnostic MUD-mode wrapper and narrow master grant now pass 16 integration
tests with actual Lima master/simuls/security, loopback peers and deterministic
pre-readiness controls. Output retains at most 512 KiB including frame headers
and 64 frames, retries rejected native writes in order and uses 8 KiB chunks;
the configured native output allowance must admit an individual chunk. Input
dispatches eight packets per batch through transactional continuations. Tests
cover maximum-size frames, accepted-peer nil ordering and independence, EOF
response drain, malformed/truncated input, consumer catches, intentional close,
aborted sends, asynchronous bind failure and foreign-caller restrictions.

The creator controls wrapper mutation; codec methods are protected, native event
pointers private, and endpoint accessors return copies. The original outgoing
privilege check remains; listening retains its existing creation permission.
The initial adapter implements MUD-mode TCP styles, with write callbacks that
notify drained output. A ten-second wrapper deadline bounds closing owners; its
cleanup path is tested by direct driver entry, without timing a real stalled expiry.
The native implementation is unchanged by this mudlib adaptation.

The complete proposed IMUD daemon now compiles after ordinary typing, callback,
class-access, timer and file-metadata adaptations. Twelve integration tests run
its real router/OOB handlers and IMAIL service against local mock peers. They
cover startup, nullable user fields while numeric zero remains an integer, mud
deletion, channel timers, router replacement/shutdown drain, authenticated file
listing and replies, mail admission/acknowledgements, unauthenticated OOB refusal
and asynchronous connection failure. A quota-exhaustion test checks listener
construction cleanup. Failed send admission retains unsent mail.
Router headers and control bodies are checked before their state updates; this
is not a complete I3 service security audit. The absent Telnet keepalive call is
removed from the I3 stream.

The coordinated thirteen-file patch is now adopted in the local Lima overlay.
A fresh full driver boot attempts 151 preloads with zero failures and completes
real Telnet account/character creation, gameplay commands and logout. A second
boot restores the account, character and router password; both boots pass local
mock-router and advertised-port OOB authentication/file-listing checks and stop
with exit zero. The restart also reproduces Lima's previously documented RST
stale-output cleanup permission failure, so a clean full restart is not established.
No RST repair or native change accompanies this adoption. Temporary loopback
configuration and runtime files are not adopted. Actual local-player mail delivery,
file put/get, other socket consumers and actual-router execution remain unestablished.

#### Lima text and binary TCP styles

The [socket wrapper][lima-imud-socket], [HTTP daemon][lima-http] and
[FTP daemon][lima-ftp] were reviewed on **6 October 2026** at the pinned Lima
revision. Extend the local wrapper with text and binary connect/listen styles
using the existing native TCP efuns. Accepted children inherit the listener's
format and deliver `(wrapper, nil)` before data. Text streams encode and decode
UTF-8, retaining partial characters across reads; binary streams deliver native
`bytes` and accept bytes or UTF-8 strings for output. Both use raw stream data
without I3 framing. Empty stream writes do nothing.

Retain the wrapper's output queue and close drain. Write callbacks may send the
next chunk themselves or return it for the wrapper to enqueue, as Lima's FTP file
producer does. Port binary consumers from `buffer` and `read_buffer` to
[`bytes`](lpc/types.md), [`read_bytes`](efun/read_bytes.md) and explicit
[`to_text`](efun/to_text.md) conversions. Wrapper support alone does not make the
HTTP or FTP daemon compatible. Their source adaptations are described below,
and their optional preload entries remain commented. Lima
supplies the older [RCP daemon][lima-rcp] as a disabled `.dontuse` file.

The one-file wrapper extension is adopted in the local Lima port. Six functional
tests cover text/binary connect and accept, split UTF-8 input, raw binary data,
queued writes, callback-produced file chunks and retained MUD framing. Wrapper
and full IMUD compilation, workspace Clippy and formatting pass. That wrapper
change leaves native TCP code and the optional service implementations unchanged.

#### Lima HTTP daemon

The [HTTP daemon][lima-http], [POST example][lima-http-form] and
[web editor CGI entry][lima-http-webed] were reviewed on **6 October 2026** at the
pinned Lima revision. Port the binary read callback to native `bytes` and replace
file `read_buffer` calls with [`read_bytes`](efun/read_bytes.md), handling its
integer-zero EOF result before sending another chunk. Use native class field
access, bare callbacks and typed nil returns.

Decode incoming bytes with [`to_text`](efun/to_text.md) using ISO-8859-1 so the
existing string parser counts one character per wire byte. Form percent decoding
retains its existing behavior. For CGI responses, apply the existing LF-to-CRLF
conversion, encode with [`to_bytes`](efun/to_bytes.md) using UTF-8, and calculate
`Content-Length` from the bytes actually sent. Static files retain their exact
bytes and file-size content length.

The daemon's POST dispatch calls `main(form, headers)`. Add an optional second
mapping parameter to the two shipped entry points while retaining their direct
one-argument use. The web editor entry continues forwarding only the form to its
application. Its application has not been validated by this source port.

The source adaptation uses the existing native TCP APIs and binary wrapper.
HTTP remains optional, with its original preload entry commented and its port
at the configured base plus three. The daemon's existing request parser and CGI
response conventions are retained, including its body-only POST response.

The three-file HTTP adaptation is adopted in the local port. Seven functional
tests pass for root/explicit HTML, exact binary image delivery, an exact file
block, zero/one-argument CGI, UTF-8 CGI content length and two-argument POST form
dispatch. Five CLI compile checks, workspace Clippy and formatting pass. Runtime
checks use lpc-rs with distinct nil, preserved call-out players and the unchanged
four-second task budget. The fixture binds loopback on an ephemeral port and
sends complete request headers; fragmented headers, the web editor application
and broader HTTP conformance remain unchecked. Native TCP, the shared wrapper,
master policy and the frozen predecessor are unchanged.

#### Lima FTP daemon

The [FTP daemon][lima-ftp] and [class/prototype header][lima-ftp-header] were
reviewed on **6 October 2026** at the pinned Lima revision. Place the header's
class declarations after the inherit. Use native class fields, typed nil returns,
bare callbacks and bound timer arguments; logging needs mixed variadic arguments.
Retain the prototypes and give the file producer a bytes result.

Keep the control stream as text and use binary styles for all data connections.
Replace buffer IO with [`read_bytes`](efun/read_bytes.md) and
[`write_bytes`](efun/write_bytes.md) under the existing session privilege. Native
byte writes require an existing file, so recreate the empty upload file after
removing an old one. TYPE A uploads retain CR removal through a reversible
ISO-8859-1 conversion; TYPE I preserves bytes. RETR retains the source's raw
file bytes and existing lack of TYPE A newline conversion. Build directory rows
with [`get_dir`](efun/get_dir.md), [`file_size`](efun/file_size.md) and
[`file_time`](efun/file_time.md), retaining the original listing formats.

Advertise the control connection's numeric local IPv4 address and wait for the
passive listener's actual bound port. The native setup is asynchronous; retain
the 40000–40100 range and ten attempts, with up to 1,000 readiness checks per
attempt at 10 ms intervals. Bind
the session into the common byte callback. Retire the one-use listener through
a subsequent call out so its accept event commits before closing. Native listener
closure discards children whose accept event has not committed, including a
child acquired inside that callback. See [TCP events](tcp-sockets.md).

The common byte callback replaces the source's separate binary passive lookup,
which uses a port key although the passive map stores control-socket keys.
That discrepancy is source-reviewed; FluffOS execution is unchecked. Close
wrappers through `remove` to drain queued replies and file data. Existing
password hashing, wizard/admin selection, anonymous settings and the optional
preload remain unchanged.

The two-file adaptation is adopted in the local port. Six functional tests pass
for anonymous control commands, passive LIST/NLST, active/passive 32 KiB RETR and
actual wizard password login with ASCII/binary STOR. The full daemon/header
compile, workspace Clippy and formatting pass. Tests use lpc-rs, distinct nil,
preserved call-out players and the four-second task budget; temporary accounts,
files and loopback/ephemeral listener settings are excluded from adoption. Native
TCP, the shared wrapper, master policy and frozen predecessor remain unchanged.
External/NAT deployments, binding failure/retry behavior, idle expiry, command
pipelining and broader FTP conformance remain unchecked.

#### Lima RST generation

The [RST daemon][lima-rst-generation] was additionally reviewed on
**5 October 2026** at the listed Lima revision. Replace its `private:` section
with individual private declarations. Directory scans use the names returned
by [`get_dir`](efun/get_dir.md), with [`file_size`](efun/file_size.md) for
directory detection and [`file_time`](efun/file_time.md) for incremental scans;
there is no metadata flag or tuple form of `get_dir`.

Use scalar [`regmatch`](efun/regmatch.md) for warning prefixes and function
prototypes. Native [`sscanf`](efun/sscanf.md) has no regex conversion, and
[`regexp`](efun/regexp.md) accepts arrays. Its indexed result puts the one-based
index before the matched string; adapt the prototype window accordingly.
Translate Spencer word boundaries to Rust regex `\b`. Copy the UTF-8 usage
text with `read_file` and overwriting `write_file`, replacing the absent `cp`.

Pass actual function values to `unguarded` and `call_out`, binding paths where
needed and using bare names otherwise. A closure such as `(: write_indices :)`
returns the function value without invoking it. Keep the existing ten-item
scan batches, filtered directories, saved modification watermark and daily
self-rescheduling sweep. [Function values](lpc/function_type.md),
[timers](efun/call_out.md).

Native validation checks annotated Unicode output, category indices, incremental
callback batches and restoring the saved watermark. A real cold boot preloads
RST and generates 468 pages containing 1,075 function entries under the unchanged
four-second task budget; HELP_D consumes the pages and saves its index.
Complete RST formatting compatibility and upstream execution remain unchecked;
this adaptation adds no native API.

#### Lima intermud mail

The [intermud mail daemon][lima-imud-mail] was additionally reviewed on
**5 October 2026** at the listed Lima revision. Its port needs the bare
`check_queue` function in both timer calls, dotted `.sender` reads from cast
`mail_msg` instances, and nil markers plus `({nil})` removal for invalid string
recipients. Keep integer IDs/timestamps and the existing hourly
self-rescheduling one-shot. [Function values](lpc/function_type.md),
[class fields](lpc/classes.md#construction-and-members),
[null values](lpc/null.md).

A real native cold boot of the subsequently adopted source preloads the daemon
with empty queues, leaving only IMUD's existing who-handler failure. Focused
tests dispatch its hourly callback twice and confirm one successor timer,
unchanged queues and no transport loading. Incoming-recipient checks preserve
the caller restriction, remove unknown To/CC/BCC names through nil markers,
exclude foreign-only recipients and leave empty lists without delivery.
Those checks use a test-only IMUD entry object and the real user registry;
restored nonempty queues, successful delivery, acknowledgements and upstream
execution remain unchecked.
The [IMUD mail module][lima-imud-mail-protocol] uses the transport/OOB machinery
whose unsupported socket dependencies are described above; empty startup does
not establish a working intermud service. This port needs no new native API.

#### Lima event and help timers

Arguments after FluffOS's `call_out` delay are callback data. Native
[`call_out`](efun/call_out.md) instead takes a repeat interval as argument three:
a positive number silently enables repetition, while a string raises an error.
Bind data explicitly, as in `call_out(&process_dir(pathname), delay)` for Lima's
help traversal. Known callbacks without bound arguments use bare names, such
as `call_out(run_scheduler, delay)`. [Upstream contract][fl-callout-reference].

For a single self-rescheduling job such as Lima's event scheduler, replace
`find_call_out("run_scheduler") == -1` with
`!query_call_out(scheduler_id)` and store the ID returned by scheduling. Declare
the handle `nosave`: it belongs to the current VM. Native one-shots are removed
before the callback executes, so the firing callback can schedule its successor.
The query also sees schedules and cancellations made earlier in the same
transaction. Keep the check after the scheduler's work so a direct invocation
still refreshes events while retaining the existing pending timer. This assumes
that all scheduling of this job updates that handle; it is not a general
replacement for name-based lookup. [Native query](efun/query_call_out.md),
[upstream lookup][fl-find-callout].

Retain self-rescheduling one-shots when that is the source's lifetime policy.
A native repeating timer survives errors thrown by a callback that started;
an uncaught error in a one-shot removes that firing and rolls back an attempted
reschedule. Repeating timers therefore change failure behavior as well as how
manual invocations interact with the schedule. [Native contract](efun/call_out.md).

Enable `LPC_CALL_OUT_PRESERVE_PLAYER=true` to retain the scheduling player,
matching Lima's enabled upstream setting. Help also retains its initiator and
can notify that object directly. Use `nil` when clearing the object or returning
an absent topic array, and `!topics` to detect an uninitialized index. The native
setting preserves timer ownership; an ordinary simul wrapper changes it.
A timer with no saved player has no owner fallback. Combat heartbeat adapters
must still establish the combat actor explicitly: the scheduling player can be
a different object. [Callback context](efun/call_out.md),
[Lima configuration][lima-timer-config].

Review completion bookkeeping when moving incremental scans to native
transactions. Help's completion used to run only from a directory callback,
leaving a flat help tree unsaved; an exception before its counter decrement
could also strand the busy state. Use shared completion for the root scan and
directory callbacks, record catchable scan failures, and let queued work drain
before releasing the busy state. Save only a successful index; a failed scan
should retain the previous save and report failure. Also catch completion
notification errors so they cannot undo the final decrement. The reviewed
source is [Lima's help daemon][lima-help-timers].

[`catch`](efun/catch.md) preserves writes and effects made before a caught error,
so directory callbacks already scheduled during a failed scan still need their
counter entries. Partial in-memory results remain visible until another rebuild;
retaining the previous saved file does not restore the previous live index.
[`save_object`](efun/save_object.md) permission and serialization errors can be
caught, but file-delivery failures after commit are logged by the driver.
This bookkeeping does not provide recovery for externally cancelled timers or
an aborted transaction that never reaches this completion routine.

#### Lima object enumeration and state scheduling

Lima's full-list `objects()` calls can use the native efun directly. Convert
predicate calls to `filter(objects(), predicate)`. `objcount` only uses its
callback to increment counters, so use a `foreach` with explicit integer
initialization instead. Domain spawn limits should count clones directly,
including surviving clones whose prototype was removed or replaced.
[Object callers][lima-state-objects], [domain counts][lima-domain-objects].

State queue entries are pairs of a target and extra data; their containing
arrays need `mixed *` declarations. Resolve path jobs when due: an empty match
set removes the job, while multiple matches must remain queued as concrete
targets until processed. Process timestamps oldest first, preserve future jobs
and unfinished work at the processing limit, and remove each current job before
calling it so callback additions and cancellations remain effective. Duplicate
checks must compare actual targets rather than collapsing different clones with
the same base name. Queue membership and ownership queries should inspect the
target slot, excluding objects present only in callback data.
[Reviewed state daemon][lima-state-objects].

Replace this daemon's heartbeat with a named repeating
[`call_out`](efun/call_out.md). A two-second initial delay and repeat interval
match [Lima's reviewed heartbeat configuration][lima-heartbeat-config]. Keep
the timer ID in a `nosave` integer and prevent recursive ticks from bypassing
the processing limit. The stateful module's deferred registration also needs
`call_out(internal_add_to_queue, 0)` in place of its string callback.
[Stateful module][lima-stateful-module].

The adaptation catches and reports each failed update, removes that job and
continues with the remaining queue. Native [`catch`](efun/catch.md) retains
writes made before the error; it does not roll back just the failed object's
changes. A whole-transaction abort still rolls back the tick, and the native
repeating timer remains scheduled. This is an explicit queue failure policy,
not automatic recovery for externally cancelled timers.

#### Lima command dispatch and stdio

Lima's [command base][lima-command-base] calls `main` with four arguments, or
with two during resend, while many concrete commands declare a private handler
with fewer parameters. Native [receiving-object resolution](lpc/inheritance.md#functions-supplied-by-the-receiving-object)
requires a visible implementation and checks calls against its definition;
ignored prototypes cannot supply a private child handler. Making `main`
protected and padding its arguments still leaves array handlers incompatible
with the base's raw-string dispatch branch.

Use a protected four-slot adapter in each command and route the base's calls
through it. The adapter calls the existing private handler with its declared
arguments; for a one-argument handler:

```c
protected varargs void dispatch_main(mixed arg, mixed flags,
                                    mixed input, mixed implode_info) {
    main(arg);
}
```

`varargs` permits the omitted slots during resend. Pass `nil` for missing
stdin. The adapter preserves `origin() == "local"`, the object caller and the
current player, but adds a local frame: caller-function/program inspection
inside `main` identifies the adapter and its source. An `evaluate(main, ...)`
callback instead reports `"function_pointer"` in the handler. Keep private
handlers and protected adapters hidden from external calls, and retain the
shell and resend guards. See [origin](efun/origin.md),
[caller inspection](efun/calling_program.md) and
[variadic parameters](lpc/variadic_parameters.md).

In [stdio][lima-command-stdio], use `nil` for nullable strings, pending command
metadata and the optional `more` continuation. Share the normal/raw initialization
path so each invocation clears its buffer, redirect target, flags and pending
metadata. Native [`explode`](efun/explode.md) retains a trailing empty element;
before passing split output to Lima's line-oriented `more`, remove exactly that
last element when the buffer ends in a newline. Preserve other empty lines,
file output and pipeline payloads.

Adapt [wish's pipeline parsing][lima-wish] together with the
[tokenizer][lima-shell-getopt] and stdio. The original stdio scan compares the
whole argument array with `"|"`, allowing later tokens into filenames; changing
only that comparison loses subsequent pipeline stages. The shell also searches
for input redirection across stage boundaries and removes tokens without their
spacing. Its intended empty prefixes need explicit empty strings/arrays because
native [negative slice endpoints](lpc/indexing.md) count from the end.
